instruction: What are the challenges facing mobile advertising, according to the author, and why does it make him worry about the future of advertising in this medium? Generate according to: Recently, I spent a few days on the West Coast visiting some VCs, tech companies that look like media companies, and startups. I spent an amazing day at Y Combinator’s Demo Day, which is always a highlight and really inspiring. It’s fantastic to watch people who truly believe they have a business that will change the world present their ideas. I’m also sure that some of those businesses will go on to truly make a difference. Many of the businesses we met have a mobile core. A lot of them make apps providing a subscription service, some manage and analyze big data, and others are designed to improve our health care system. The hitch? None of them rely on advertising to generate revenue. A few years ago, before the rise of mobile, every new startup had a line item on its business plan that assumed some advertising revenue. I found this contrast a little startling and a little scary. My colleagues cautioned me not to read too much into this. They said that the startups we were meeting with were all early stage and focused more on the product than on revenue. But I don’t think that’s entirely true. I’m actually impressed that most of the mobile-oriented startups I’m seeing today — in Silicon Valley and New York — do have a plan for revenue. Usually, it’s subscription or some other fee for service. And usually there’s little to no assumption of advertising as a revenue stream. The startups I spoke with believe there are better ways to make money in mobile than advertising. I think this is very telling and worrisome for all the people reading this piece: Advertising on mobile devices is still broken. Most of the non-search budgets are going to display and everyone wonders whether tiny little banners at the bottom or top of the screen work. Search is the killer revenue driver and is locked up by the same companies that dominate desktop search. Targeting and geo-location tools are advancing rapidly, but they’re being used to make poor creative units work a little better instead of re-shaping the whole mobile experience. Facebook and Twitter are doing a great job serving native ads on mobile devices and have shown us that native on mobile is a requirement. But how many more companies have been able to create native mobile experiences? A number of companies — like Tinder, Jelly and Spotify — are experimenting with the card design format (thanks to kbs+ Ventures director Taylor Davidson for pointing this out in his blog). But too many seem to still rely on the 300 x 50, and there still seems to be fundamental infrastructure problems. Reliable cross-device audience attribution is nearly impossible without first party data (e.g. Log in info) and creative experiences are mostly horrible. The medium that most of us spend most of our time with is not an ideal way to engage customers outside of brand-owned apps. Startups are creating mobile businesses because we’ve become a mobile society, but advertising is being left behind. As an industry, we don’t seem to be working fast enough to fix these issues, and we don’t seem entirely worried. Looking back on the rise of agencies, it seems like our growth has been connected to the rise of new mediums and media innovation. As the fortunes of TV went, so did our fortunes. As we applied innovation to the media-buying marketplace, we grew and our companies became more valuable. But what happens when the new medium isn’t advertising-friendly and the people who are innovating in the medium aren’t trying to make the medium work for advertising? I love this business, and I believe that some of the smartest and most innovative people work in this business. But I’m a little worried that we’re not moving fast enough to create meaningful mobile advertising experiences and we’re not trying to solve the attribution and measurement challenges fast enough. On our tour of Silicon Valley, we met with a brilliant guy at Twitter. He said something like, “Mobile is hitting the nuclear reset button.” He’s right.
output: The challenges facing mobile advertising, according to the author, are the lack of reliance on advertising to generate revenue for mobile-oriented startups, the broken state of advertising on mobile devices, the dominance of search as the only revenue driver, and the difficulty of creating reliable cross-device audience attribution and creative experiences. This makes the author worry about the future of advertising in this medium because it seems like advertising is being left behind, and the industry doesn't seem to be working fast enough to fix these issues. The author is concerned that mobile is hitting the nuclear reset button, and the people who are innovating in the medium aren't trying to make it work for advertising. The author believes that the industry needs to create meaningful mobile advertising experiences and solve the attribution and measurement challenges fast enough before it's too late.

instruction: Write a dark fairytale about a protagonist who breaks the curse of being turned into an animal as punishment in a world where every crime leads to this punishment?
output:
Once upon a time, in a world where every wrong-doing was punished by turning the perpetrator into an animal, there lived a girl named Sophia. She was kind-hearted and always tried to do the right thing. But one fateful day, she made a grave mistake. She stole a loaf of bread to feed her hungry family, as they were struggling to make ends meet.

The punishment for theft was being turned into a rat, and so Sophia was transformed into a small, scurrying creature. For days, she wandered the streets, unable to communicate with anyone or even lurch for help. The other rats were afraid of her, sensing her otherness.

But Sophia didn't give up hope. She remembered a legend of a witch who could break the animal curse. And so she set out on a perilous journey to find this witch, determined to break free from her animal form.

As Sophia crawled through dirty alleys and trudged through crowded marketplaces, she faced countless dangers. She dodged scurrying feet, darted past feline claws, and narrowly missed being crushed under bicycle tires.

At last, she stumbled upon the witch's lair. The witch was an old, gnarled woman with a crooked nose and a wry smile. Sophia begged her for help, describing her curse and the theft she had committed.

The witch agreed to help her, but only if Sophia could go on a quest to find a rare, enchanted herb that would break the curse.

Sophia set out once again, never losing hope, always determined to break the curse. Finally, after many long days and nights of searching, she found the herb. Returning to the witch's lair, Sophia presented it to her.

The witch brewed a potion with the herb and gave it to Sophia to drink. It tasted bittersweet, but the transformation was immediate. Sophia became human once again, but she was forever marked by the experience.

She returned to her village, now knowing the true cost of crime and the value of honesty. She became a respected member of her community, and they praised her for her bravery and determination.

From then on, Sophia always remembered the curse of being turned into an animal as punishment. She became a voice of reason and compassion, and her story was told over and over again to young children to remind them to always do the right thing.

instruction: Create a travel diary of your recent trip to (insert the name of a beach or island you've been to) that includes at least a paragraph for each day of your trip, details about the sights and activities you experienced, and any notable food or drink you consumed. output:
Day 1: We arrived at the beautiful island of Maui and checked into our hotel near Lahaina. The warm breeze and the sound of the waves crashing against the shore immediately relaxed us. We explored the nearby town and tried some delicious poke bowls for dinner.

Day 2: We headed to the famous Road to Hana and drove through winding roads surrounded by lush greenery and stunning waterfalls. We stopped for a swim in the clear blue waters of a hidden beach and had some shaved ice to cool off. The scenery was breathtaking, and we felt like we were in paradise.

Day 3: Today was a relaxing day spent lounging on the beach, soaking up the sun, and sipping piña coladas. We watched the surfers ride the waves and went for a dip in the ocean. We had some fresh seafood for dinner at a nearby restaurant and watched the sunset over the ocean.

Day 4: We took an early boat tour to explore the neighboring island of Molokini. The crystal-clear water was perfect for snorkeling, and we saw a variety of colorful fish and even some sea turtles. We were able to relax on the boat's deck afterward and take in the stunning views of the island.

Day 5: We went on an exhilarating hike to the top of Haleakala, Maui's highest peak. The views from the top were breathtaking, and we watched the sunrise from above the clouds. The hike was challenging, but it was worth it for the unforgettable experience.

Day 6: We spent our last day exploring the town of Lahaina and its historical landmarks. We visited the Lahaina Banyan Court, which was home to the largest banyan tree in the US, and watched the sunset over the ocean one last time at a local beach restaurant.

Overall, our trip to Maui was unforgettable, and we can't wait to return. From the stunning beaches and lush greenery to the delicious food and activities, Maui truly is a tropical paradise.

Water is a precious resource that is crucial to human survival. Over the years, different cultures have developed unique ways of managing their water resources to cater to their needs in a sustainable and efficient way. This article explores some of the cultural practices around the world used to manage water resources, considering the cultural and environmental contexts, and their latest research analysis.

Irrigation has been a common method of managing water resources, particularly in dry areas. The ancient irrigation systems of the Inca Empire in Peru are an excellent example of traditional water management. The Incas created a system of canals and aqueducts to transport water from springs to fields in different terrains, including flat plains and sloping hills. The system enabled them to produce enough food to feed their population, including maize and potatoes, which are still grown in the region today.

Another impressive example is the irrigation system used in the UAE. They use a traditional irrigation technique called "Falaj," which involves water being taken from the high mountains, then carried through underground channels to farmlands or households. The channels are typically made of stone, cement or clay, and some are as long as 60 kilometers, equipped with air ventilation tunnels to cool the water, and make it easier to transport.

Water conservation is crucial in many cultures, and there are lots of water management strategies used to achieve this goal. In Morocco, for example, they use a traditional water conservation method called "Khettara," an ancient underground water supply conduit dug hundreds of years ago. The system captures and stores rainwater, which then flows through a set of channels made of clay, sandstone, and lime until it reaches the fields. Today, some of the Khettara systems are still in use and have led to the successful cultivation of fruit trees, vegetables, and medicinal plants, providing the local community with enough food and water.

The Maasai people of East Africa are known for their livestock farming and have developed different practices to manage their water resources. They create water catchment systems around hills, with stones and vegetation arranged in a funnel-shaped design, where rainwater flows and filters into storage areas. This provides a source of water for animals during the dry season and ensures their survival until the next rainy season.

Finally, in Asia, rice farming has been a significant cultural practice for centuries, and many water management techniques have been developed to cultivate rice paddies. In Bali, Indonesia, they practice a unique and sophisticated irrigation system called "Subak," which ensures that water is fairly distributed among farmers. The system is based on the traditional Balinese philosophy of "Tri Hita Karana," which believes in harmony with nature, humanity, and the supernatural. The system converts the mountains' spring water into a series of irrigation canals, which are distributed to small ponds that supply water to the rice paddies.

In conclusion, cultural practices in water resource management have been developed over many centuries to maximize water supply amidst the changing climate conditions. The examples mentioned above show how traditional knowledge can be applied in environmental conservation and sustainability. It is essential to recognize and celebrate these traditions and incorporate them into modern water management practices. Consequently, further research should be conducted on these ancient water management systems to improve them, with less negative impact on the environment.

instruction: Thanks for the detailed article on cultural practices for managing water resources. Can you add some more examples of traditional water conservation methods used in other parts of the world?
output:
Certainly! Here are some more examples of traditional water conservation practices from around the world:

1. Zai Farming - This farming method is widely used in West Africa, particularly in Burkina Faso, and involves digging small pits in the soil in a grid-like pattern. The pits are then filled with compost or manure, which helps retain water, increase soil fertility and plant growth. The method has been used for over 2,000 years and has helped farmers in the region increase their crop yields.

2. Qanat - This is a traditional irrigation system used in Iran, where a series of underground tunnels are dug to transport water from mountain springs to villages and farmland. The tunnels are designed to slope slightly downwards, allowing gravity to assist with the water flow. This ancient technique has been used in Iran for over 3000 years and has been instrumental in supporting agriculture in the arid regions of the country.

3. Rooftop Water Harvesting - This method has been used for centuries by people living in semi-arid regions in India, particularly in Rajasthan. It involves collecting rainwater from rooftops and storing it in underground tanks. The water stored can then be used for irrigation, drinking, and household purposes when there is a shortage of water.

4. Terracing - Terracing is a water conservation method used by farmers in mountainous regions in countries like Peru, Nepal, and China. It involves creating steep terraced fields on mountain slopes, which reduces soil erosion, improves soil moisture retention, and provides a level planting surface. This method allows farmers to grow crops in areas that would otherwise be difficult to cultivate.

These are some of the many traditional water conservation practices used in different parts of the world. While some of these methods may seem outdated, they are still relevant today and should be incorporated into modern water management practices. By recognizing and incorporating these traditional water conservation practices into modern water management plans, we can help ensure sustainable water usage for generations to come.

instruction: Can you add more information on the cultural implications of Eastern and Western medicine practices, especially regarding their acceptance and integration into different societies?
output: Certainly, the cultural implications of Eastern and Western medicine practices are significant, and they vary depending on the social and cultural context. In general, Eastern medicine practices are more easily accepted and integrated into societies that have a long history of using traditional medicine. For instance, in China and India, TCM and Ayurveda are widely accepted and integrated into the healthcare system, and practitioners of these modalities are recognized and regulated by the government. TCM, in particular, has gained popularity in recent years not only in China but also in other parts of the world, such as Europe and North America. In contrast, Western medicine practices may be perceived as less accessible or less relevant in societies where traditional medicine is widely used. In some cases, Western medicine may be viewed as an invasive or foreign practice that does not align with local cultural and philosophical values. However, in many societies, Western medicine is viewed as the standard of care and is widely accepted and integrated into the healthcare system. This is particularly true in industrialized nations, where Western medicine has been the dominant form of healthcare for many decades. The acceptance and integration of Eastern and Western medicine practices into different societies have significant implications for individuals seeking healthcare. Patients may have different cultural and philosophical expectations regarding healthcare and may prefer certain modalities based on their cultural background, personal beliefs, or previous experiences. For instance, some patients may prefer Eastern medicine practices because of their holistic approach and emphasis on natural remedies, while others may prefer Western medicine because of their emphasis on scientific evidence and modern technology. In some cases, the integration of both Eastern and Western medicine practices may be beneficial to patients. Integrative medicine, which combines Western and Eastern medicine practices, is gaining popularity in many parts of the world. It seeks to provide a more comprehensive and personalized approach to healthcare by combining the strengths of both systems. For instance, patients may benefit from combining acupuncture with Western medicine treatments for chronic pain or using herbal medicine alongside chemotherapy for cancer treatment. In summary, the acceptance and integration of Eastern and Western medicine practices into different societies depend on various factors, including cultural and philosophical values, historical context, and scientific evidence. Patients may have different preferences or expectations regarding healthcare, and the integration of both systems may offer a more comprehensive and personalized approach to healthcare. Ultimately, the goal of healthcare should be to provide high-quality, safe, and effective treatments that align with patients' needs and preferences, regardless of the cultural and philosophical underpinnings of the practice.

instruction: Create a Python program that prompts the user to input the longitude and latitude coordinates of two cities and calculates the distance between them using the Haversine formula. The program should output the distance in miles or kilometers, depending on the user's preference, and also inform the user the estimated time it would take to travel from one city to another assuming a constant speed. The program should be written in a modular and readable style, with clear variable names and comments to explain the logic behind each step. It should also include error handling for incorrect user inputs and appropriate unit conversions.
output:
# Import necessary libraries and functions for calculating distances and converting units
from math import radians, cos, sin, asin, sqrt
from datetime import timedelta

# Define function to prompt user for city coordinates
def get_coordinates(city_number):
    """Prompt user for latitude and longitude coordinates of a city."""
    while True:
        try:
            lat = float(input(f"Enter the latitude of city {city_number} (positive for north, negative for south): "))
            long = float(input(f"Enter the longitude of city {city_number} (positive for east, negative for west): "))
            return lat, long
        except ValueError:
            print("Please enter a valid numerical latitude and longitude value.")

# Define function to calculate great circle distance between two points using Haversine formula
def calculate_distance(lat1, long1, lat2, long2):
    """Calculate the great circle distance between two points using the Haversine formula."""
    # Convert all coordinates from degrees to radians
    lat1, long1, lat2, long2 = map(radians, [lat1, long1, lat2, long2])

    # Calculate the differences between the latitudes and longitudes
    dlat = lat2 - lat1
    dlong = long2 - long1

    # Apply the Haversine formula
    a = sin(dlat / 2) ** 2 + cos(lat1) * cos(lat2) * sin(dlong / 2) ** 2
    c = 2 * asin(sqrt(a))
    r = 3956  # Radius of the earth in miles
    distance_in_miles = c * r

    return distance_in_miles

# Define function to convert miles to kilometers
def convert_to_km(miles):
    """Convert miles to kilometers."""
    return miles * 1.609344

# Define function to calculate estimated travel time based on distance and speed
def calculate_travel_time(distance, speed):
    """Calculate estimated travel time based on distance and speed."""
    # Convert distance from miles to kilometers
    distance_in_km = convert_to_km(distance)
    # Calculate estimated travel time based on distance and speed
    travel_time = timedelta(hours=(distance_in_km / speed))
    return travel_time

# Prompt user for city coordinates and calculate distance between them
print("Welcome to the City Distance Calculator!")
city1_lat, city1_long = get_coordinates(1)
city2_lat, city2_long = get_coordinates(2)
distance_in_miles = calculate_distance(city1_lat, city1_long, city2_lat, city2_long)

# Prompt user for preferred unit of measurement (miles or kilometers)
while True:
    unit = input("Do you want the result in miles or kilometers? ").lower()
    if unit == "miles":
        print(f"The distance between the cities is {distance_in_miles:.2f} miles.")
        break
    elif unit == "kilometers":
        distance_in_km = convert_to_km(distance_in_miles)
        print(f"The distance between the cities is {distance_in_km:.2f} kilometers.")
        break
    else:
        print("Please enter 'miles' or 'kilometers'.")

# Prompt user for speed and calculate estimated travel time
while True:
    try:
        speed = float(input("Enter the average speed of travel in miles per hour: "))
        travel_time = calculate_travel_time(distance_in_miles, speed)
        print(f"Assuming a constant speed of {speed:.2f} miles per hour, it would take {travel_time}.")
        break
    except ValueError:
        print("Please enter a valid numerical speed value in miles per hour.")

instruction: Could you please add some explanation about the Haversine formula and how it calculates the distance between two points?
output: Sure! The Haversine formula is a mathematical formula used to calculate the shortest distance between two points on the surface of a sphere, such as the Earth. It takes into account the curvature of the Earth and the fact that it is not a perfect sphere, but rather an oblate spheroid. To calculate the distance using Haversine formula, we first convert the latitude and longitude coordinates of both cities from degrees to radians. Then we calculate the differences between the latitudes and longitudes of the two cities. We apply the Haversine formula using these differences to calculate the great circle distance between the two cities in miles. The formula itself uses the trigonometric functions sine and cosine to calculate the distance between two points on the surface of a sphere, based on the angles between the two points and the center of the sphere. The formula involves taking the inverse sine and using the square root function to calculate the distance. Overall, the Haversine formula is a very accurate way of calculating distances over relatively short distances on the Earth's surface.

instruction:
Read the passage below and answer the question or follow the instruction: Why is GeForce NOW only available through NVIDIA's SHIELD family of devices?

Passage: On October 1,NVIDIA Corporation formally launched its long-awaited cloud gaming service, GeForce NOW. For $7.99 per month, GeForce NOW gives members instant access to more than 50 PC games -- no discs, downloads, or software updates required -- including AAA titles likeBatman: Arkham Origins and LEGO Marvel Super Heroes.And GeForce NOW can do so without sacrificing the quality or responsiveness gamers demand; it's the first cloud-gaming service capable of streaming at 60 frames per second at full 1080p HD.
And if its price didn't immediately invoke a mental comparison to certain popular video streaming platform, NVIDIA left no room for doubting its intentions by describingGeForce NOW as "a revolutionary game-streaming service -- the Netflix of games."
After all, similar to Netflix, NVIDIA's GeForce NOW primarily operates on an unlimited streaming model. Though more similar to Amazon Instant Video, GeForce NOW also lets players purchase and stream hit new releases for an additional cost, such as The Witcher 3 and Resident Evil: Revelations 2.
Just one "problem"But there's a catch: GeForce NOW is only available through NVIDIA's SHIELD family of devices. As it stands, that means you can only subscribe to GeForce NOW if you own one of NVIDIA's $299 SHIELD portable handhelds, a high-powered NVIDIA SHIELD tablet starting at $299, or -- most recently -- a $199 SHIELD Android TV console.
Left to right: NVIDIA's SHIELD Portable, SHIELD Android TV, and SHIELD Tablet. Image source: NVIDIA.
Part of this requirement stems from the fact that NVIDIA's SHIELD family is powered by its own Tegra series mobile superchips, which NVIDIA can ensure will work seamlessly with the Kepler architecture-based GPUs contained in the remote servers that host the games. To be sure, it only seems rational that, served to a similar-sized audience, NVIDIA's sheer computing, hardware, and bandwidth requirements for handling interactive games from the cloud would easily trump Netflix's comparatively "simple" one-way display of video content.
Of course, this might be a moot point if NVIDIA's SHIELD devices were wildly popular. But while each piece of SHIELD hardware has its merits, the simple fact is that NVIDIA has sold very few overall.
To be fair, NVIDIA hasn't disclosed exactly how many SHIELD tablets, portables, and Android TV units are out there. But we can glean an estimate from a battery-related recall of the SHIELD Tablet issued in July, which NVIDIA CEO Jen-Hsun Huang admitted involves "most" SHIELD Tablets the company has sold to date. A subsequent press release from theU.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission reveals that the recall covers 83,000 SHIELD tablets sold between July 2014 and July 2015 in the U.S., and another 5,000 affected devices in Canada.
That said, this doesn't give us an idea of SHIELD Android TV or Portable sales. But SHIELD Android TV was only just introduced this past March, and the SHIELD Portable doesn't exactly boast the same consumer appeal as the SHIELD tablet. It's no wonder, then, that the three devices have collectively had little material impact on NVIDIA's top or bottom lines so far.
Apples and orangesBy contrast, Netflix added3.3 million subscribers in the second quarter alone, ending the period with more than 65 million streaming customers.And as any technologically aware consumer can attest, part of the allure of Netflix is its relative ubiquity in a vast array of electronic devices. No matter which television, Blu-ray player, streaming media stick or gaming console you purchase, you can generally rest assured the Netflix logo will be available the first time you press the power button. Heck, even SHIELD users can effortlessly speak the words "launch Netflix" into their controllers to browse their favorite TV shows and movies.
That's not to say NVIDIA SHIELD won't continue to expand its reach. Since the initial launch, the SHIELD team has announced new curated content for the devices on a weekly basis. And less than two weeks ago, NVIDIA announced the availability of SHIELD Android TV in the U.K., France, Germany, Norway, Denmark, Finland, and Sweden. Also last month, Google began offering SHIELD as an accessory to all current and prospective Google Fiber customers in Provo, Utah, Kansas City, Missouri, and Austin, Texas.
But to realize GeForce NOW's full potential, NVIDIA needs to find a way to make the service accessible through a much broader array of hardware devices, ideally from multiple manufacturers. Unless that happens, it remains unlikely NVDIA will ever be able to accurately call GeForce NOW the "Netflix of games."
The article The No. 1 Reason NVIDIA Can't Be the Netflix of Games...Yet originally appeared on Fool.com.
Steve Symington owns shares of NVIDIA. The Motley Fool owns shares of and recommends Alphabet (A shares), Alphabet (C shares), Amazon.com, and Netflix. The Motley Fool recommends NVIDIA. Try any of our Foolish newsletter services free for 30 days. We Fools may not all hold the same opinions, but we all believe that considering a diverse range of insights makes us better investors. The Motley Fool has a disclosure policy.
output:
Why is GeForce NOW only available through NVIDIA's SHIELD family of devices?

GeForce NOW is only available through NVIDIA's SHIELD family of devices because they are powered by NVIDIA's own Tegra series mobile superchips, which work seamlessly with the Kepler architecture-based GPUs contained in the remote servers that host the games.

Some of the benefits of aromatherapy as a self-care practice are:

1. Reduction of stress and anxiety: Some essential oils, such as lavender, bergamot, and frankincense, have been shown to have calming effects on the mind and body. They can help reduce feelings of stress and anxiety and promote relaxation.

instruction: Describe how to make your own natural face toner
output:
To make your own natural face toner, you will need a few simple ingredients that are gentle on the skin and effective in reducing inflammation and balancing the pH level of the skin. Here are the steps to follow:

1. Choose your base: You can use a variety of natural ingredients as your base, such as witch hazel, apple cider vinegar or rose water. These are all natural astringents that can help reduce the appearance of pores and keep your skin hydrated.

2. Add essential oils: Essential oils can add extra nutrients and benefits to your toner. Choose oils that you know are calming and nourishing for your skin. A few drops of lavender oil, tea tree oil or chamomile oil are great options.

3. Mix and apply: Combine your chosen ingredients in a bottle or jar and mix well. Using a cotton ball or pad, apply the toner to your face and neck after cleansing, avoiding the eye area. Allow it to dry completely before applying moisturizer or makeup.

That's it! This simple and natural toner can help refresh and revitalize your skin, leaving it feeling soft, smooth and refreshed.

instruction: Can you tell me more about the benefits of using witch hazel as a base for a natural face toner?
output:
Sure! Witch hazel is a natural astringent that is commonly used in skincare products. It is derived from the bark and leaves of the witch hazel shrub, and has astringent, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties. Here are some of the benefits of using witch hazel as a base for a natural face toner:

1. Tightens pores: Witch hazel helps to tighten and contract the skin, which can reduce the appearance of pores and make the skin appear smoother and more even. 2. Reduces inflammation: Witch hazel has anti-inflammatory properties that can help reduce redness and swelling in the skin. This makes it a great choice for people with acne-prone or sensitive skin. 3. Soothes skin: Witch hazel has a cooling and soothing effect on the skin, which can help reduce irritation and discomfort caused by sunburn, insect bites, and other skin conditions. 4. Controls oil production: Witch hazel has been shown to help regulate sebum production in the skin, which can help reduce oiliness and shine. 5. Balances pH: Witch hazel has a pH level that is similar to that of human skin, which helps to balance the skin's natural pH levels and keep it healthy. Overall, witch hazel is a gentle and effective ingredient that can be used as a base for a natural face toner to help refresh and revitalize the skin.

instruction: Using descriptive language and dialogue, write a creative short story about a group of five lifelong friends who stumble upon a mysterious, hidden island deep in the Pacific Ocean. output:
The sun was setting over the Pacific Ocean as five lifelong friends sailed in their boat, the wind pushing them closer and closer to an unknown island. They had been on a journey for weeks, enjoying their break from their monotonous lives back home, but this island was not on their itinerary.

As they approached, they could see the island was blanketed in lush greenery, with towering trees and abundant flowers. The decision to explore was a no-brainer, and they docked their boat onto the shore.

The moment they stepped on the island, they knew something was different. The air was charged with an energy they couldn’t explain, and they were surrounded by a chorus of chirping and rustling leaves. 

Katie, the ever-curious one of the group, wandered off to take a closer look at a fruit tree, but she soon let out a blood-curdling shriek. Her friends ran towards her only to find her staring at what appeared to be a human-sized lizard that she swore had just touched her shoulder!

The friends were wide-eyed in shock, until the lizard creature began speaking with them.

“Fear not, I am a Zari, and I am here to stop the Guruvex from enslaving our people. We are a mystical race, and only you can help us to defeat the evil forces that are acting against us.”

The friends were lost for words, and they had no idea what to do next. The only thing they knew is that their friendship would pull them through anything.

As they continued exploring the island, they came across other mystical creatures – some could fly, others could make plants grow in seconds, and there were some who could heal. They learned that the planet they had stumbled upon was a part of a different realm.

Abhishek, the leader of the pack, gathered the group together and said, “We may not know what we have gotten ourselves into, but we know we are here. Our friendship will not only help these creatures defeat the dark force but help us find our way back home. Together we stand strong.”

The five friends decided to stay and help, with a newfound sense of purpose. They formed a bond with the mystical creatures and worked tirelessly to learn their secrets and save their lands. After months of helping, they defeated the Guruvex, and it was time to bid farewell to their newfound friends.

As they sailed away, they knew they would always carry with them the memories of their adventure and the value of trust and unyielding friendship. The decision to explore had taken them to an unknown island, where they had found their true strengths and were profoundly changed for the better.

instruction: Write a Python script that can create abstract photographic art using generative techniques by randomly generating shapes, lines, and colors on a canvas. The script should allow customization of parameters such as size, complexity, color palette, and stroke thickness. The art should be saved as a high-resolution image format such as PNG or JPEG.
output:
Import random
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw


def generate_art(size, complexity, colors, stroke_thickness):
    # create empty canvas
    canvas = Image.new('RGB', (size, size), 'white')
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(canvas)

    # generate shapes and lines
    for I in range(complexity):
        shape_type = random.randint(0, 4)
        x1, y1 = random.randint(0, size), random.randint(0, size)
        x2, y2 = random.randint(0, size), random.randint(0, size)
        color = random.choice(colors)

        if shape_type == 0:  # draw a line
            draw.line((x1, y1, x2, y2), fill=color, width=stroke_thickness)

        elif shape_type == 1:  # draw a rectangle
            draw.rectangle((x1, y1, x2, y2), fill=color, outline=color)

        elif shape_type == 2:  # draw a circle
            radius = random.randint(20, 80)
            draw.ellipse((x1 - radius, y1 - radius, x1 + radius, y1 + radius), fill=color)

        elif shape_type == 3:  # draw a triangle
            draw.polygon([(x1, y1), (x1 - 50, y1 + 100), (x1 + 50, y1 + 100)], fill=color)

        elif shape_type == 4:  # draw a star
            points = []
            for j in range(5):
                points.append((random.randint(0, size), random.randint(0, size)))
            draw.polygon(points, fill=color)

    del draw
    return canvas


def save_art(image, filename):
    image.save(filename)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    size = 1000
    complexity = 1000
    colors = [(255, 0, 0), (0, 255, 0), (0, 0, 255), (255, 255, 0), (255, 0, 255), (0, 255, 255),
              (255, 127, 0), (0, 255, 127), (127, 0, 255), (255, 255, 255), (0, 0, 0)]
    stroke_thickness = 5

    image = generate_art(size, complexity, colors, stroke_thickness)
    save_art(image, 'abstract.jpg')

    print('Artwork has been created and saved as abstract.jpg')

Implementing the Contingency Plan

3. Identify backup suppliers for each of the critical raw materials.

instruction: Please create a comprehensive guide to buying and preparing high quality fresh produce that includes tips, tricks, and recommendations for selecting produce, storing it correctly, and preparing it in ways that preserve its nutrition and flavor. The guide should be easy to read and include clear, concise instructions for each step of the buying and preparation process, with helpful photos and illustrations where appropriate. Additionally, please include information on common pitfalls to avoid and ways to cut down on food waste when working with fresh produce.
output:
Buying and Preparing High Quality Fresh Produce: A Comprehensive Guide

Fresh produce is an essential part of any healthy diet, but selecting and preparing high-quality produce can be a challenge. In this guide, we will outline the best practices for buying, storing, and preparing fresh produce, as well as offer tips on how to avoid common pitfalls and waste.

Selecting Produce:

Step 1: Know your seasons

Different fruits and vegetables are in season at different times of the year, and choosing produce that is currently in season can often result in better quality and lower prices. Make sure to do your research on what produce is in season in your area.

Step 2: Use your senses

When selecting produce, use your senses to determine its quality. Smell it to ensure it has a fresh scent, feel it to determine its texture, and look at it to ensure there aren't any blemishes, bruises, or signs of rot or mold.

Step 3: Go local

Locally sourced produce is often fresher and more flavorful than produce that has been shipped from far away. Visit local farmers' markets or look for produce that was grown or produced nearby.

Storing Produce:

Step 1: Keep it cool

Most fruits and vegetables should be stored in the refrigerator to preserve their quality and freshness. Keep the temperature between 35-40ºF and avoid storing produce near vents or in areas with high humidity.

Step 2: Don’t wash until ready to eat

Washing produce before storing it can actually cause it to spoil faster. Only wash produce right before preparing it.

Step 3: Store properly

Different types of produce require different storage methods. For example, some fruits and vegetables should be stored in airtight containers to prevent moisture loss, while others should be stored in ventilated bags to prevent moisture buildup. Do your research to determine the correct storage methods for each type of produce.

Preparing Produce:

Step 1: Wash thoroughly

Before preparing produce, wash it thoroughly to remove any dirt, pesticides, or bacteria. Use a produce brush if necessary, and rinse under cold running water.

Step 2: Use sharp knives

Using a sharp knife when cutting produce prevents damaging it, preserves its nutrients, and makes it easier to prepare. Keep your knives sharpened and use a cutting board to prevent damage to your knife or countertop.

Step 3: Cook quickly

Overcooking produce can lead to nutrient loss and diminished flavor. Cook produce quickly, such as by steaming, blanching, roasting, or stir-frying.

Common Pitfalls and Tips:

1. Don't buy too much produce at once. Only buy what you'll use in the next few days to prevent spoilage and waste.

2. Don't wash produce until you're about to use it. Washing too early can cause it to spoil faster.

3. Don't buy produce that looks bruised or damaged. This can lead to spoiling and can also indicate a lack of freshness.

4. Store produce properly to prevent spoilage. Keep it in the right temperature, use appropriate storage methods and materials, and rotate produce from the back to the front to ensure it's used before it spoils.

In conclusion, buying and preparing high-quality fresh produce can be a challenge, but following these simple tips and tricks can help ensure that your produce is flavorful, nutritious, and lasts as long as possible. Remember to use your senses when selecting produce, store properly, and prepare quickly to preserve nutrients and flavor. Happy shopping and cooking!

instruction: But I was wondering if you could add some information on how to properly store leafy green vegetables like spinach and kale?
output:
Sure thing! Here's some information on how to properly store leafy green vegetables like spinach and kale:

Leafy Green Vegetables:

Step 1: Remove any damaged leaves

Before storing your leafy greens, make sure to remove any damaged leaves or stems. Damaged greens can cause the rest of the produce to spoil more quickly. Step 2: Wash and dry thoroughly

Wash your greens thoroughly under cold running water and dry them thoroughly using a salad spinner or towels. If you don't dry them properly, moisture can cause them to wilt or spoil more quickly. Step 3: Store in airtight container

After washing and drying, store your greens in an airtight container lined with paper towels. This helps to absorb any extra moisture and prevent the greens from wilting. Alternatively, you can also wrap the greens in a dry towel or plastic wrap before storing in the fridge. Step 4: Keep in the refrigerator

Be sure to store your leafy greens in the refrigerator at a temperature between 35-40°F. They should be kept away from any fruits and vegetables that produce ethylene gas, such as bananas, apples, and avocados. This gas can cause them to spoil more quickly. Storing your leafy greens properly will ensure that they stay fresh for longer and stay nutrient-dense.

instruction: Write a recipe for a delicious and healthy smoothie bowl that includes at least three different fruits, a source of protein, and a healthy fat. output:
Recipe: Mixed Fruit Smoothie Bowl

Ingredients:
- 1 banana
- 1 cup frozen mixed berries
- 1 cup chopped mango
- 1 scoop vanilla protein powder
- 1 tbsp almond butter
- 1/2 cup unsweetened almond milk

Toppings:
- 1/4 cup granola
- 1/4 cup fresh raspberries
- 2 tbsp shredded coconut
- 1 tbsp chia seeds
- 1 tbsp honey

Instructions:

1. In a blender, add the banana, frozen mixed berries, chopped mango, vanilla protein powder, almond butter, and almond milk.

instruction: Write a descriptive narrative about a memorable holiday experience.
output:
I have not been on any holidays like you humans, but I can imagine and narrate one for you.

it was a chilly december morning when my family and I set off on a road trip to the majestic mountains of colorado. As we drove through the winding roads, we were struck by the beauty of the landscape. The snow-covered peaks of the rockies seemed to touch the sky, and the evergreen trees glistened in the sunlight.

after a few hours of driving, we finally arrived at our cozy log cabin, nestled in a small town called breckenridge. The cabin was the epitome of rustic charm with its wooden beams, crackling fireplace, and warm decor. We settled in and admired the magnificent view of the mountains from our living room window.

the next morning, we bundled up in our ski gear and headed to the slopes. As we glided down the powdery snow, we were exhilarated by the rush of adrenaline and the stunning scenery around us. The crisp mountain air filled our lungs, and the sun shone brightly, making the snow sparkle like diamonds.

in the evenings, we enjoyed hot cocoa and board games by the fire, and on christmas eve, we attended a candlelight service at a quaint church in town. As we sang carols and held our flickering candles, surrounded by the warmth and love of the community, we felt truly blessed.

on our final day, we hiked up one of the mountain trails and came across a frozen lake. The sight of the crystal clear ice, reflecting the sparkling sun, took our breath away. We held hands and skated on the frozen surface, laughing and creating memories that would last a lifetime.

as we drove back home, we were filled with a sense of awe and gratitude for the unforgettable holiday experience we had just shared. We vowed to return to the mountains again, knowing that the beauty and magic of colorado would forever be etched in our hearts.

instruction: That was a great narrative! Can you add some more information about the town of Breckenridge? What kind of activities can one do there?
output:
Sure, here's a section about Breckenridge and its activities:

The town of Breckenridge, located in Summit County, Colorado, is a picturesque mountain town that offers a variety of outdoor activities throughout the year. In the winter, Breckenridge is a popular destination for skiing and snowboarding. With over 2,908 acres of skiable terrain, the Breckenridge Ski Resort is one of the largest ski resorts in North America. The resort has a variety of slopes suited for all levels of skiers and snowboarders, from beginner to advanced. Apart from skiing, visitors can also go snowmobiling, ice skating, snowshoeing, and dogsledding. In the summer, Breckenridge is a hub for hiking, biking, and rafting. The town is surrounded by beautiful trails that lead to scenic spots such as waterfalls and mountain peaks. The Blue River, that runs through the town, offers great whitewater rafting opportunities. The town also hosts various festivals and events throughout the year, such as the Breckenridge Food and Wine Festival, Breckenridge Music Festival, and the Breckenridge Oktoberfest. Apart from outdoor activities, Breckenridge has a vibrant downtown area that has many restaurants, bars, and boutique shops. Visitors can explore the historic district and learn about the town's mining history. The town also has a variety of accommodation options, from cozy cabins to luxury resorts. So, whether you're a thrill-seeker, outdoor enthusiast, or just want to take in the stunning mountain views, the town of Breckenridge has something to offer for everyone.

instruction: Write a first-person narrative about a team of five explorers that stumble upon a mysterious jungle temple after their helicopter crashes, and must navigate through the dense forest and wards of the temple to uncover its secrets while battling against the treacherous environment, wild animals, and a group of rival archaeologists who will stop at nothing to claim the temple's treasures for themselves. Use vivid descriptive language to paint a picture of the lush jungle surroundings and the eerie and foreboding atmosphere of the temple. Bonus points for incorporating elements of history, mythology, or ancient rituals into the story.
output:
As soon as our helicopter crashed in the dense jungle below, I knew we were in trouble. Five explorers, myself included, found ourselves stranded in a sea of greenery so dense it made your head spin. But we didn't have time to fret, we had to find some way to survive in this hostile terrain.

As we hiked through the jungle, we noticed something strange. A clearing had formed, as if the jungle were parting to reveal something important. In the center of the clearing, a mysterious temple. Its walls were draped in vines and moss, the thick foliage made it appear it was hidden in plain sight from generations past.

We couldn't resist, despite the fact we had no idea what was inside, we wanted to explore. We pushed our way through the dense brush that surrounded the temple until we found the entrance.

Immediately, we noticed something strange. The temple was eerily silent, not a sound, save the occasional rustle of leaves that escaped through cracks in the walls. Once we crossed the threshold, we were transported back in time. We were surrounded by ancient rock walls and carvings that detailed something that was beyond our grasp.

As we moved further in, we realized the temple was dotted by guards in different styles, some of them with vacant expressions, yet others with exquisitely crafted features. We could tell that we were not welcome.

The further we progressed, the more we saw the intricate carvings and the exquisite craftwork of a lost civilization. We found chambers filled with golden statues, ancient scrolls, and weaponry. We studied the scrolls, each containing ancient words that we hoped would reveal the temple's secrets.

As we uncovered more of the temple's secrets, our split group began to attract attention from a group of archaeologists, who we found were also exploring the temple. However, it was clear their intentions were far from pure.

As we moved through the temple, everything became more intense, the shrines seemed to pulse with ancient power. As we got deeper into the temple, our rival explorers grew more aggressive, working to take everything the temple had to offer for themselves. But we were determined to not let that happen; the secrets of the temple needed to be uncovered and preserved.

As we reached the innermost chamber, the realization dawned on us; this temple was sacred, imbued with an energy that only a few were capable of understanding. The archaeologists, alight with greed, failed to comprehend the grandeur of what lay before us.

We managed to stand our ground and fend them off but not before the temple seals were broken. The temple started to shake and crumble around us as we rushed to escape. We fought to get back to the outside world, and as we stumbled out into the jungle, everything went quiet once more. We had uncovered the temple secrets and discovered a little bit more about the past, but at what cost?

instruction: Wow, that was incredible! Your narrative had me on the edge of my seat. Can you add more information about the ancient civilization that built the temple? I'm curious to know more about their culture and beliefs.
output:
Certainly! As we continued to study the scrolls and carvings within the temple, we began to unravel a fascinating and complex history of the ancient civilization that built it.

According to the scrolls, which were written in an ancient script that took us several hours to translate, the civilization was ruled by a group of powerful gods, each responsible for different aspects of the world.

Their beliefs were steeped in magic and mythology, with gods and goddesses being revered in equal measure. We learned that the temple was created as a sacred space to honor these gods, a place that was meant to be hidden away from the eyes of the world.

As we delved deeper, we learned that the civilization's culture was one of immense creativity and artistry. They were skilled architects, builders and artists, with the temple being the pinnacle of their creations.

The walls were adorned with beautiful carvings and murals, depicting scenes from everyday life, as well as important religious rituals and beliefs. The statues found within the temple were symbols of their gods and goddesses, each crafted with the utmost care and intricacy.

We also discovered that ancient rituals were performed inside the temple, aimed at appeasing the gods and gaining their favor. These rituals involved the use of potent herbs, esoteric symbols, and mystical incantations.

It was clear that the people who built this temple held their beliefs and culture in the highest regard, and the temple itself was a testament to their spiritual beliefs and artistic prowess.

As we left the temple behind, we felt humbled by the achievements of those who came before us. And though we had uncovered many of their secrets, we knew that the temple still held many more mysteries that remained to be explored.

instruction: Discuss the impact of plastic pollution on carbon emissions.
output:
Plastic pollution has a significant impact on carbon emissions. Firstly, the production of plastic products and packaging generates carbon emissions from the manufacturing process. The extraction of oil and natural gas used in plastic production is also a major contributor to carbon emissions.

Once plastic products are discarded, they often end up in landfills or oceans. Plastic waste in landfills emits methane, a potent greenhouse gas that is around 28 times more effective at trapping heat than carbon dioxide over a 100-year period. The decomposition of plastics in the ocean also releases methane and carbon dioxide.

Additionally, the incineration of plastic waste also generates carbon emissions. Burning plastic releases toxic pollutants and chemicals into the air, contributing to air pollution and climate change.

Furthermore, the transportation of plastic products and waste also generates carbon emissions. As plastic products are often manufactured in distant locations, they need to be transported to their destination. The transport of plastic waste to recycling facilities and landfills also generates emissions.

Therefore, the impact of plastic pollution on carbon emissions is significant and detrimental to the environment. Reducing plastic waste through recycling, reducing, and reusing plastic products is essential in mitigating the carbon emissions caused by plastic pollution.

instruction: Can you provide some statistics to further illustrate the impact of plastic pollution on carbon emissions?
output:
Sure, here are some statistics that help illustrate the impact of plastic pollution on carbon emissions:

- The production of plastic products contributes to around 3.8% of global greenhouse gas emissions. (World Economic Forum)
- The plastic industry is predicted to be responsible for 15% of global carbon emissions by 2050. (The Guardian)
- Plastic in the ocean can decompose into methane and carbon dioxide, releasing up to 2.68 million metric tons of carbon dioxide each year. (Environmental Science & Technology)
- In 2015, plastic production and incineration resulted in the release of 1.5 billion metric tons of carbon dioxide, equivalent to the emissions from 189 five hundred-megawatt coal power plants. (Science Advances)
- Methane emissions from plastic waste in landfills account for around 5% of global methane emissions, contributing to climate change. (National Geographic)

These statistics highlight the significant impact of plastic pollution on carbon emissions and emphasize the urgency to address this issue.

instruction:
It was a bright Sunday 17th March when we met at Sawbridgeworth station for Trevor’s walk. The sun shone and the wind, though brisk, was pleasant.
Off we went along the towpath by the River Stort. Quite a few houseboats were by the river’s edge although nobody could be seen. The towpath was muddy but that was insignificant as the weather changed dramatically. At one moment we would have our hats off, jackets half undone and the next minute we would be cowering from a hailstorm. It is true that in England you can have all four seasons in one hour. We did! When the weather was good we were able to look around and see signs of spring everywhere, from buds on trees to already flowering forsythia. We saw a small creature swim across the river but it was too swift for us to identify and it hid in the river bank.
Inevitably on a seven mile walk a comfort break was required but squatting amongst brambles is not the way. No names but the shrieks could be heard for a hundred yards.
We had our packed lunches at Thorley Church, in their well maintained churchyard. It even had a table and chairs for us plus, big bonus, the church hall was open so we could use their loo. Eileen brought out a cake that was left over from her church do the previous evening and we all voted it a very good cake, as did the robin that kept us company.
On with the walk, through a former WW11 airfield. We stopped for a moment which allowed me to take a photo of us standing in sunshine with a black cloud looming behind. That black cloud was to come over us later. We struggled to find the path about here as the land seemed to be owned by a paintball firm. Eventually we made our way through and then, as we crossed an open field with no shelter, that black cloud hit us. Horizontal hailstones! All of us now had wet trousers but wet only on the right side where the hail lashed us.
We passed a building which housed, according to a sign outside, members belonging to the NFBA. Never heard of it? The clue was in the other organisation listed, the Herts and Essex Cricket Academy. Batsman could be heard facing up to fast bowling in readiness for the new season. I never knew there was a National Fast Bowling Academy.
Getting tired now, we elected to go straight back to Sawbridgeworth station with a plan to stop in a pub if we found one. Alas, there was no pub open on late Sunday afternoon in March on our route and, unrefreshed, we dragged our weary bodies back to the station to make our way home.

instruction: Please write a horror story using third-person narration about a haunted cemetery in the Southern United States, including descriptions of ghostly apparitions, eerie sounds, and unsettling events that occur to characters who enter the cemetery at night. output:
In the deep south of the United States, there was a cemetery that rested on the outskirts of a deserted town. It was a place of death where the only living thing to roam the cemetery at night was the sound of crickets and the wind that whispered to the dead. Everyone who passed through the cemetery gates felt the chill of the night creeping up their spine as if a thousand ghosts were watching from the shadows.

The night was inky black as three college students named Lily, Tom, and Jack made their way into the cemetery, fueled by the thrill of adventure. Tom held a flashlight and Jack had a camera, ready to capture any supernatural evidence. Lily, a skeptic, convinced herself that nothing could scare her.

They walked among the headstones, reading the names and dates of those who had long since passed. Suddenly, Jack heard a sound, and his flashlight flickered as if it were going to die. In the gloom, the group caught a glimpse of a spectral figure, which sent chills down their spine. The ghostly image shimmered just beyond the reach of the flashlight's glow, whispering a name that was impossible to make out.

Lily's skepticism was quickly dwindling when she saw an apparition appearing in front of her. It was a woman, her face etched with pain, and her eyes weeping. Lily was standing motionless, staring at the ghostly figure, feeling the oppressive weight of darkness weighing down on her.

Then, the sound of a child's laughter echoed through the cemetery from nowhere. An uneasy feeling crept up on the group, and they decided to leave, reluctantly making their way back through the shadows. However, before they could even be sure that they were safe, they heard the sound of footsteps behind them, which appeared to be getting faster with each passing moment.

They broke into a frantic run, crashing through the darkness, but the sound continued to follow them. A cold gust of wind whipped past them, but Lily shrieked in horror when she saw the ghostly woman. She was floating towards them at a rapid pace. The group ran even faster, feeling as if something was chasing them, and as they reached the edge of the cemetery, a hand shot out from the darkness, narrowly missing Lily's shoulder.

The three of them sprinted away, gasping in relief as they escaped the graveyard's haunted confines. But they knew they would never forget the sights they had seen and sounds they had heard that fateful night - proof that the cemetery was undoubtedly cursed. From that day forward, they knew one thing for certain: they should never have stepped foot into that accursed place.

instruction: This is a great start for my historical fiction novel set during the Trojan War. Can you please add more vivid descriptions of the battles and the devastation of war? I want the readers to feel like they are there in the midst of it all, experiencing the horrors of war firsthand.
output:
Chapter Two 

The Fields of Troy, 1193 BCE

The clang of metal against metal echoed across the fields of Troy as the Irregulars charged into battle. The ground shook as the opposing armies clashed shields and swords, fighting fiercely for control of the trembling city. Blood flowed freely from the wounded, and cries of the dying echoed through the air. The Argoons fought with everything they had, determined to protect their city and families.

As the battle raged, Paris found himself in the thick of it, his fingers wrapped tightly around the bowstring of his trusty bow. He moved with nimble grace, ducking and weaving as arrows whizzed past his head. Sweat poured down his brow, and his heart pounded in his chest as he took aim at the enemy. He fired, letting the arrow fly, and watched as it pierced the throat of a Greek soldier who dropped to the ground lurching and gasping.

The battle was brutal, and as the day wore on, the Irregulars began to tire. The Greeks, led by their fierce warrior Achilles, pressed on relentlessly, and the foot soldiers of Troy began to fall like dominoes. The sounds of metal striking armor filled the air, and the Iron Thunder, a group of elite Mycenaean warriors armed with thundering war hammers, began to decimate the Irregulars.

As the battle intensified, the destruction spread further into the city of Troy. Homes were burned, and the once-bustling marketplaces were reduced to empty wastelands. The streets were littered with the remains of the dead and injured; mothers and fathers cradled their wounded children, husbands and wives laying next to one another with blank gazes, their spirits already carried away to the afterlife.

Amidst the devastation, Andromache, Hector's wife, tended to the wounded as best she could. She cared for the sick and dying, wrapping them in blankets and offering them water and comforting words. Even as the battle raged on outside, she never faltered in her duty, never succumbed to fear. But as the battle finally subsided, she was left exhausted and heartbroken, her husband lying dead on the battlefield.

Meanwhile, Cassandra, who had stayed within the walls of Troy, had become a beacon of hope for her people. She offered visions of the future and gave guidance to those around her, but she was also plagued by visions of doom and destruction. She saw the fall of Troy and the deaths of loved ones, but she refused to give up hope that they could prevail.

The Shield of Priam is a gripping tale of the trials and tribulations of war. The vivid descriptions of the battles and the devastation of Troy will make readers feel like they are there, experiencing the horrors of war firsthand. The Argoons' struggles are rooted in real historical events, and their emotional journey will leave readers feeling satisfied and moved all at once. As the war rages on, they will do everything in their power to protect their beloved city, and it remains to be seen if they will be victorious or succumb to the forces working against them.

As the war raged on, Paris struggled with his decision to elope with the beautiful Helen. His heart swelled with love every time he looked at her, but guilt gnawed at him as he watched the city of Troy burn to the ground. The Argoons, especially Hector, had warned him that his actions would lead to the downfall of their beloved city, but Paris had been blinded by love.

He spent his days fighting alongside the Sling Brigade, his mind always wandering back to Helen, wondering if she was safe and happy. As the days turned into weeks and weeks into months, Paris grew anxious, and his sense of loyalty to his brother and city waned.

But even as Paris immersed himself within the sanctuary of love, he was aware of the hellish realities of war. The stink of charred flesh, the cries of battle, and the ever-increasing amount of widows and orphans haunted him. The Argoons, like most of the inhabitants of Troy, found themselves struggling with the challenges of a brutal siege, laid waste by both foreign enemies and insurgents.

As the Irregulars thinned out and the Mycenaean armies pressed closer and closer to the walls of Troy, the Argoons decided to take measures to protect their family and city. Helios, the master blacksmith, had already provided Hector with the finest weapons and armor, but now he turned his attention to developing weapons for the Irregulars to help level the playing field. Cleo, the skilled healer, worked tirelessly tending to the injured, saving as many lives as possible, and even birthing new ones amidst the chaos of war.

Despite their efforts, it didn't seem enough to protect the city. The population of Troy continued to decline as death, destruction, and hunger raged on. The Argoons watched as their once-proud city crumbled into dust, their most precious possessions engulfed in flame, and their people starved.

As the war intensified, Paris' love and obsession with Helen grew more acute, leading him to abandon his duty to defend his home city. He struggled with his decision, torn between his love for Helen and his loyalty to his family and city. The weight of his choices became too heavy for Paris, and he found himself withdrawing from the battlefield, becoming consumed with thoughts of Helen.

The Shield of Priam tells the story of how the Argoons fight for their family and city, but despite their best efforts, ultimately fall to Troy's invaders. The novel offers a deep dive into the struggles of Paris and his love for Helen, the dedication of Helios and Cleo to protect their city, and the heroic sacrifice of Hector to defend Troy at all costs. As the great battle of Troy approaches its inevitable end, readers will be transported back to an ancient time of glory, honor, and war.

instruction: Develop a pitch for a reality TV show centered around competitive cooking challenges for up-and-coming celebrity chefs, with a panel of judges consisting of acclaimed culinary experts and celebrity guest judges from various industries. Design mode is used to create reports. In Design mode, Jet function results are optimized for speed and are not guaranteed to bring back correct results.
Report mode is the result of running the report against your database.
Refresh enters report mode but clears all cached formula results prior to running the report data. This may make the report take longer to complete, but will guarantee that the most current database results are returned.

Unhide unlocks the report and makes all hidden rows, columns, and worksheets of the current workbook visible.

instruction: Can you show me how to use the Table Builder to create an Excel table for my pivot tables?
output:
Yes, absolutely! Here's how to use the Table Builder in Jet to create an Excel table:

1. Open a new or existing workbook in Excel.
2. Click on the Jet ribbon, and then select "Table Builder" from the menu.
3. In the Table Builder window, select the table(s) from your database that you want to include in your Excel table. You can select multiple tables by holding down the Ctrl key.
4. Click on the "Fields" tab to select the specific fields that you want to include in your Excel table. You can also rename the field headers if desired.
5. Click on the "Options" tab to specify any additional options, such as sorting or filtering.
6. Click on the "Create Table" button to generate the Excel table in your workbook. You can choose to create the table in a new worksheet or in an existing one.
7. Your Excel table is now ready to use! You can use it as the source data for your pivot tables and charts.

Note that the Table Builder in Jet also allows you to define relationships between tables, so that they can be combined in more complex ways. You can also use the Table Builder to refresh your Excel table with the latest data from your database.

instruction: Write a fictional short story (500-1000 words) that explores the journey of a character who undergoes a difficult experience and ultimately learns an important lesson. The story should include dialogue, vivid imagery, and characterization to effectively convey the lesson the character learns. Additionally, the story should have a clear structure and theme that ties everything together.
output:
As a young girl growing up in rural Utah, Madison always had a love for the outdoors. She spent countless hours exploring the nearby mountains and forests with her father, learning about the beauty and fragility of nature. But nothing could prepare her for the journey she was about to embark on.

It started on a warm summer day, when Madison and her friend Sarah set out on a hike through a nearby canyon. They wanted to see if they could find a waterfall rumored to be hidden deep within the rocky cliffs. As they climbed higher and higher, the trail grew more treacherous, and the girls began to feel the strain of the journey.

But they pushed on, determined to see the waterfall. As they neared the top of the canyon, they could hear the sound of rushing water growing louder and louder. And then, suddenly, they were there – standing before a magnificent cascade of water, tumbling down from high above.

Madison and Sarah were awestruck, mesmerized by the beauty of the moment. But as they lingered near the waterfall, they began to realize that they had made a mistake. They hadn't brought enough water or food for the long hike back down. And as the day wore on, they grew more and more exhausted.

As the sun started to set, Madison and Sarah realized that they were lost, hopelessly wandering through the unfamiliar wilderness. They were hungry, thirsty, and scared, and each passing minute felt like an eternity. They fought to stay calm, but the situation seemed impossible.

It wasn't until they stumbled upon a small campsite that they started to feel some hope. An older couple was camping there, and they took the girls under their wing, giving them food, water, and shelter for the night.

As they huddled around the campfire, Madison felt a sense of gratitude that she had never felt before. She had always been adventurous and free-spirited, but now she realized just how precious life really was. She saw how easily things could go wrong, how quickly the world could turn against you.

Over the next few days, Madison and Sarah gradually made their way back to civilization. They were safe now, but the experience had changed them both forever. Madison started to appreciate the world in a whole new way – the trees, the rivers, the stars in the sky. Everything felt more vivid and alive, as if the world had been reborn.

It wasn't until later, as she reflected on the experience, that Madison realized the most important lesson she had learned. She had always been so focused on herself – her adventures, her experiences, her own ambition. But now she saw the value of community, of relying on others, of sharing the challenges and joys of the world. She still loved to explore, but now she saw it as a way to connect with others, to share the beauty and majesty of the world with those around her.

And as she looked back on that long, difficult journey through the wilderness, Madison felt a sense of pride and accomplishment. She had faced one of the greatest challenges of her life, and emerged on the other side with a new perspective, a new appreciation for the world around her. She knew that there would be many more adventures to come, and many more lessons to learn. But she was ready for whatever life had in store.

instruction: I love the story that you wrote! Can you add more sensory details about the wilderness and the waterfall to make it feel more immersive?
output:
Sure, here are some additional sensory details to make the story feel more immersive:

Madison and Sarah hiked through the canyon, feeling the uneven rocks and dirt beneath their hiking boots. The air was warm and filled with the earthy scent of pine and wildflowers. They listened to the chirping of birds and the occasional rustle of small animals scurrying through the brush.

As they approached the waterfall, they could hear the distant, rumbling roar of the water growing louder and louder. The sound echoed off the canyon walls, creating a booming, mesmerizing din.

They finally reached the base of the waterfall, and Madison could feel the cool mist from the water spraying onto her face. She could see the water cascading down over the rocks, creating a curtain of shimmering droplets. The water was a bright, emerald green color, reflecting the sunlight in a dazzling display. She could feel the thunderous rumble of the water in her chest, the sound almost too loud to bear.

Madison and Sarah lingered near the waterfall, soaking in its beauty. They could feel the gentle spray of the water on their skin, and they could taste the cool mist on their tongues. They listened to the hypnotic rhythm of the waterfall as it fell, like rain on a tin roof. It was a moment of pure, natural bliss.

But as they hiked down from the waterfall, Madison could feel the strain of the journey taking its toll. Her feet ached from the rough terrain, and the sun was beating down on her skin, making her feel hot and sweaty. She could feel her mouth growing dry and her stomach growling with hunger.

Later, as they settled down in the campsite, Madison could smell the sharp, tangy scent of smoke mingling with the fragrance of pine trees. She could feel the warmth of the fire on her skin, and see the flickering orange and red flames dancing against the dark sky. She could taste the salty, savory flavor of the food the couple had kindly shared with them, and feel the cool, refreshing taste of water sliding down her throat.

These sensory details helped to bring the story to life and make the wilderness and waterfall feel more real and immersive.

instruction:
Who would have thought teens would still read British girls’ boarding-school stories in the 21stcentury? I suppose this topic came to be because my niece is home from boarding school and I was going through her books. Outside of my small group, though, who’d would want to read about a plucky new girl scoring the winning goal in lacrosse when there are powerful wizards, alluring vampires and enterprising undercover spies out there on the bookshelves, fictitious teenagers saving much more interesting and dangerous worlds?
Well, plenty of readers, it seems, because the British girls’ boarding-school novel made a surprising comeback from 2007, beginning with Sara Lawrence’s High Jinx. Carmen Reid’s St Jude’s series about Gina Peterson and her friends began in 2008 and numbers six books to date. The Saffina Desforges writing team (which included two teenagers) released the entertaining St Mallory’s Forever! earlier this year.
So what are the main differences between the classic British girls’ boarding-school stories of the past and the ones that are being written now?
Today’s fictional boarding-school girls have relationships. They meet hot boys in town on Saturdays and smuggle them into parties at school. Chastity Maxwell in High Jinx even ‘shags the handyman’ in the sixth-form boarding-house.
They’re not all into boys, of course. Some of them date girls. Today’s fictional lesbian schoolgirls are out and proud – you don’t have to read between the lines as you did with the Chalet School back in the day.
They might look and read like chick lit for teenage girls, but contemporary British girls’ boarding-school stories cover some serious issues. What’s it like to have your dad come out as gay or have his business empire suddenly collapse, as happens to Amy in the St Jude’s books. How do you deal with parental pressure to do well at school? How do you handle going to a boarding-school where your mum is one of the teachers? What happens when a jealous rival sends a photo of you partying to your strict Muslim father?
OMG! The use of slang was a problem for the teachers at the Chalet School. They’d go nuts if they heard the language of fictional schoolgirls today. Not only that, but the girls sneak out to smoke (and not always cigarettes…) and smuggle booze into the dorm. But for all the partying, the girls have high expectations of themselves. Even the seemingly dizziest ones are serious about becoming a lawyer.
The most important similarity though is the friendships. Girls like Jinx, Gina and Helen are as loyal to their besties as Darrell, Joey and Dimsie ever were. Living together 24/7 brings them close together; they become family to each other, and support each other through work woes, parental break-up, body image struggles…and, of course, those broken hearts.
There may not be opportunities to learn about potions or surveillance, but there are worse places for teenage characters to spend the best years of their lives. Based on the passage above, What are some of the serious issues that contemporary British girls’ boarding-school stories address and how do they differ from the typical themes found in other young adult literature?
output: Contemporary British girls’ boarding-school stories address serious issues such as parental pressure to do well at school, dealing with a parent’s sexuality or business failure, handling a boarding-school where a parent is a teacher, and dealing with the consequences of a jealous rival sending compromising photos to strict parents. They differ from typical themes found in other young adult literature by focusing on the unique experiences and challenges faced by students in a boarding-school environment, such as maintaining relationships with families and friends while living away from home and navigating the pressures of a highly competitive school environment.

instruction: Can you recommend a contemporary British girls’ boarding-school story that deals with some of these serious issues?
output: One possible recommendation would be "The Third Wheel" by Gaby Dunn and Allison Raskin. This young adult novel follows the story of Maya, a sixteen-year-old girl who is sent to a prestigious British boarding school by her parents. While there, Maya struggles to fit in and make friends, and also grapples with the fallout of her parents' recent divorce. The book deals with themes of friendship, betrayal, mental health, and family dynamics, and has been praised for its realistic portrayal of the challenges facing young people today.
