instruction: What are some traditional Polish dishes to try in Lublin?
output:
1. Pierogi – dumplings stuffed with various fillings such as minced meat, cabbage and mushrooms or fruit.
2. Bigos – a hearty stew made with different types of meat, sauerkraut, onion, mushrooms and various spices.
3. Kielbasa – Polish sausage made with pork, beef, or turkey, and flavored with garlic and other herbs and spices.
4. Golabki – cabbage leaves stuffed with a mixture of meat, rice, and vegetables.
5. Zurek – a sour rye soup served with sausage and hard-boiled egg.
6. Kotlet schabowy – breaded pork cutlet served with potatoes and vegetables.
7. Sernik – a type of cheesecake made with quark cheese.
8. Makowiec – a poppy seed cake typically eaten during Christmas and Easter.
9. Babka – a sweet yeast cake flavored with vanilla or lemon zest.
10. Faworki – deep-fried twisted pastries dusted with powdered sugar.

instruction:
Here is a piece of text: Hyped and heralded as the worst film ever made, there’s no getting round the fact that cult phenomenon The Room is a terrible movie that’s fascinating precisely because of the singular, bizarre vision of its creator, Tommy Wiseau. An accidental auteur of awfulness, his own semi-mythical status – no one seems to know exactly how old he is, where he’s from or how he made his money – has seen him likened to a modern day Ed Wood, the sort of figure whose artlessness has become an art form in its own right. What’s never been entirely clear, though, is how willingly Wiseau has embraced his film’s so-bad-its-good reputation. Sure, he’s managed to seize victory from the jaws of defeat by exploiting the willingness of fans to pack out late-night screenings and buy up The Room-related merchandise. But having poured his heart and six million dollars into the supposedly semi-autobiographical film, it must have stung to discover everyone just wanted to laugh at him.
Wherever the truth lies, he’s found a somewhat sympathetic champion in James Franco, whose new film The Disaster Artist dramatises the making of Wiseau’s magnum opus, turning the story behind it into funny but poignant tale of creativity and commitment in the absence of talent. Franco, who also directed the film, throws himself into the role too, treating Wiseau almost as a living art installation – there to disrupt and challenge the normal way of doing things, whether he’s making a movie, dancing in a club or hanging out with his best friend Greg Sestero (Dave Franco), a young aspiring fellow actor he meets in an acting class in San Francisco and promptly moves to LA with in order to pursue their shared dream of stardom together.
With both facing regular rejection, Tommy writes The Room as a showcase for both of them and promptly finances it himself, assuming complete creative control before anybody comprehends how lacking in basic filmmaking skill or acting ability he really is. The making of the film becomes a catalogue of hilarious mishaps, mistakes and misguided creative decisions. Even if you haven’t seen it, the shared incredulity of the cast and crew (played by a roster of A-list comedy and acting talent, including Seth Rogen, Alison Brie and Jackie Weaver) is not exaggerated: the film they’re making really does beggar belief. If you have seen The Room there’s additional joy in seeing the meticulous behind-the-scenes recreations of its most meme-worthy moments.
Nevertheless, the film isn’t just a series of potshots at a Wiseau. Franco is a bit of restless talent himself (he’s racked up 36 directing credits in the last decade, mostly for films no one has seen) and he’s sensitive to the way Tommy’s attempts to express himself are sometimes misguided attempts to replicate work he admires. One of the most famously bad scenes in The Room, for instance, has its origins in Rebel Without a Cause, and you start to feel for Tommy when you realise he’s trying to do James Dean without realising how melodramatic Dean’s line readings sounds by modern standards.
The film is full of grace notes like that. On one level it functions as a useful demolition job on the artist-as-savant myth that too many films and documentaries indulge, but on another it’s a reminder that even bad art can spring from and inspire compelling human stories.
Happy End is Michael Haneke’s latest ironically titled exercise in cinematic hostility and, in some respects, it’s very much business as usual as he starts picking once again at the scab of bourgeois privilege. But if this has made his films a little tiresome of late, there’s something divinely unsettling about this new one. Like Benny’s Video and Hidden, it begins with a queasy moment of surveillance, with Haneke finding new ways to ratchet up fears about the use of social media before zeroing in on another wealthy dysfunctional family, this one living in the shadow of the immigration crisis in Calais. Blithely indifferent to the suffering of anyone outside their immediate circle, and barely on speaking terms with each other, the family – presided over by Isabelle Huppert’s no-nonsense matriarch –seems to be one tiny act of aggression away from imploding altogether, something Haneke turns into a satirical comment on the futility of trying to maintain such a broken social system.
“When there’s a choice between being right and being kind, choose kind,” says a character in Wonder. No doubt the filmmakers will be hoping anyone who sees this heart-tugger about a facially deformed kid will follow suit, embracing the many positive messages it espouses rather than focusing on the many broadly manipulative ways it tries to extract tears from you. Caked in prosthetics, Room’s Jacob Tremblay is fine, if a little cloying, as its ten-year-old hero, but the film relies on Julia Roberts and Owen Wilson (cast as Auggie’s over-protective parents) doing their twinkly movie-star thing instead of exploring the family’s situation in any meaningful way.

Based on the text material above, generate the response to the following quesion or instruction: What are some criticisms of Michael Haneke's film Happy End and how does it differ from his previous works?
output: Some critics have found Michael Haneke's film Happy End to be another exercise in his familiar theme of picking at bourgeois privilege. However, there is a new unsettling quality to this film, with Haneke finding new ways to ratchet up fears about the use of social media and focusing on a wealthy dysfunctional family living in the shadow of the immigration crisis in Calais. The family seems to be on the brink of implosion, creating a satirical comment on the futility of trying to maintain a broken social system. Despite this, the film has been criticized as being tiresome due to its familiar theme.

John Deere has introduced a complete range of advanced technology fairway, tees & surrounds and rough mowers for 2014, based on extensive feedback from greenkeepers and other golf and turf industry professionals.
Common features across the new A Model range include a brand new TechControl display, LoadMatch from the John Deere compact tractor range, internal wet disc brakes and improved operator stations – all engineered to provide users with greater control of the machines, easier operator training and best in class cut quality.
All A Models also feature OnCourse Technology, which intelligently integrates electronic controls with the mowers’ mechanical features to deliver improved performance, better diagnostics, more uptime and increased reliability, productivity and operator comfort.
The simple to use, password protected TechControl display enables the course manager, head greenkeeper or deputy to quickly set or change mowing, turning and transport speeds, for example, to limit variations in performance by different operators and provide a more consistent, quality finish. On-board visual diagnostics and the ability to set regular service times also help to maximise productive time.
A popular feature adopted from the John Deere compact tractor range is LoadMatch, which automatically adjusts the speed of the machine to deliver consistent power to the cutting units during heavy load conditions. This is also designed to maximise productivity and maintain high levels of cut quality.
In addition to these key systems on every model, the 7500A, 7700A and 8700A PrecisionCut and the 7500AE hybrid electric fairway mowers feature an improved operator station, with multiple step locations making it easy to get on or off the mowers from either the front or rear. Tyre alignment has also been improved to deliver an even after-cut appearance across the mowing pass.
The 8000AE hybrid mower features 18in QA5 (Quick Adjust) cutting units, which narrows the overall cut width to produce tighter striping and superior cut quality, with even fewer hydraulic leak points. The three-wheel design of the 8000AE offers greater manoeuvrability and quicker turns than traditional four-wheel machines, for maximum productivity.
In addition, the new A Model E-Cut hybrid electric fairway mowers can be set to automatically deliver reduced engine speed during mowing, with fuel savings of up to 30 per cent.
The new John Deere 7200A PrecisionCut, 7400A TerrainCut and 8800A TerrainCut tees & surrounds and rough mowers also share many of the same features as the new fairway mowers. Both the 7200A and 7400A are equipped with a new larger eHydro transmission and redesigned wheel motors for improved traction performance, especially on slopes, while the 8800A is equipped with a new 55hp four-cylinder engine producing over 27 per cent more power.
Each machine in the new A Model line-up is produced using an updated assembly process at John Deere’s Turf Care facility in North Carolina, USA. The process incorporates advanced manufacturing technologies such as smart tools and vision systems to provide consistent build quality across the range.
John Deere has also announced updates to the 2653B PrecisionCut tees & surrounds mower and the 2500B PrecisionCut and 2500E hybrid electric greens mowers for 2014.
To improve operator comfort, particularly during long working hours, the 2653B now features a lower seating position and increased leg room, while a new double-acting steering cylinder enables the operator to achieve straighter cut lines with less effort.
In addition, the 2500B and 2500E models now incorporate electric controllers to provide increased diagnostic capabilities using the Control Area Network or CANbus system, as used since 2009 on John Deere’s E-Cut hybrid electric fairway mowers. output: John Deere's new A Model range of golf and turf mowers includes fairway, tees & surrounds and rough mowers, all with a brand new TechControl display, LoadMatch, internal wet disc brakes, and improved operator stations. OnCourse Technology integrates electronic controls with the mowers' mechanical features to improve performance, diagnostics, uptime, reliability, productivity, and operator comfort. The TechControl display allows course managers to quickly set or change mowing, turning, and transport speeds, while LoadMatch adjusts the speed of the machine to deliver consistent power to the cutting units. Other features include improved operator stations, tyre alignment, Quick Adjust cutting units, a three-wheel design for greater manoeuvrability, and reduced engine speed during mowing to save fuel. The new A Model range is produced using an updated assembly process incorporating advanced manufacturing technologies for consistent build quality. Updates have also been made to the 2653B and 2500B PrecisionCut and 2500E hybrid electric greens mowers for improved operator comfort and diagnostic capabilities. Overall, John Deere's new A Model range delivers greater control, easier operator training, and best in class cut quality for improved performance, productivity, and operator comfort.

One example of a successful creative who uses meditation is Arianna Huffington. Founder of HuffPost, Arianna is a staunch advocate for meditation in the workplace. She believes that it has not only helped her creatively, but also helped her become a more effective leader. Famed film director David Lynch, known for his avant-garde films and surreal aesthetic, has also been a vocal advocate for meditation. He says it helps him tap into his creative energy when working on new projects.

Scientific evidence has shown that meditation helps to increase our ability to generate new ideas, think outside the box, and improve problem-solving skills. Meditation has been found to increase the grey matter in the prefrontal cortex, which is responsible for decision making, emotional regulation, and cognitive control. A study in the journal PLOS ONE showed that participants who meditated for just two weeks scored higher on creativity tests than those who didn’t.

Meditation doesn’t have to be a complicated process. Setting aside just five to ten minutes every day to focus on your breathing, and clear your mind can bring about significant results. Many successful people have incorporated meditation into their daily routines. Oprah Winfrey takes at least 20 minutes a day to meditate, while Steve Jobs used meditation to help clear his mind and stay focused while working on new projects.

So how can you incorporate meditation into your daily routine to unleash your creativity? Start small. Begin with just a few minutes each day, working up to longer sessions as you become more comfortable. Find a time of day that works best for you, whether it’s first thing in the morning, during your lunch break, or right before bed. Use guided meditations to help focus your mind, and give yourself permission to let go of any distractions.

Incorporating meditation into your daily routine can improve your creativity and problem-solving skills, reduce stress and anxiety, and lead to a more fulfilled and balanced life. Who knows, a few mindful minutes a day could be the key to unlocking your true potential. Give it a try, and let the magic of meditation inspire you to greatness.

def generate_password(length, uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols, ambiguous):

  else:
    characters = string.ascii_uppercase + string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + string.punctuation

  if not uppercase:

instruction: Could you provide a brief overview or summary of Hermes' role as the messenger of the gods?
output: Hermes is a Greek god who is often associated with communication, trade, travel, and messenger services. He is the son of Zeus and the Titaness Maia, and he has served as the messenger of the gods in many stories and myths. In this role, he is responsible for carrying messages from the gods to the mortals and vice versa, and he is often depicted as a messenger in artwork and literature. Hermes is also known for his quick wit and ability to outsmart opponents, as well as his role as a guide and protector for travelers. Overall, Hermes' role as the messenger of the gods represents the importance of clear communication and the exchange of ideas and information.

instruction: That's interesting. Can you tell me about any specific myths or stories where Hermes served as the messenger of the gods?

Certainly! There are many stories in Greek mythology where Hermes served as the messenger of the gods. Here are a few notable examples:

1. In the Homeric Hymn to Hermes, one of the most famous stories about Hermes, he is born in a cave and quickly demonstrates his cunning and skill by stealing Apollo's cattle. When Apollo confronts him about the theft, Hermes denies any knowledge of it, but the gods eventually discover the truth. As a punishment, Hermes is forced to return the cattle and make a lyre for Apollo, which he does using a turtle shell and strings from the cow's intestines. Apollo is so enamored with the instrument that he forgives Hermes and makes him his personal messenger.

2. In the story of Perseus and Medusa, Hermes helps Perseus in his quest to slay the monstrous monster Medusa. Hermes gives Perseus his winged sandals to help him travel quickly to the Gorgon's lair, and also provides him with a sickle to behead her.

3. In the story of Orpheus and Eurydice, Hermes acts as a guide leading Orpheus to the Underworld so he can try to rescue his wife Eurydice. Hermes helps Orpheus navigate the perilous realm and instructs him to not look back as he leads Eurydice back to the world of the living. Tragically, Orpheus looks back at the last moment and loses Eurydice forever.

There are many more stories about Hermes as the messenger of the gods, but these are a few notable examples!

instruction: Write a 500-word narrative with a third-person point of view about a character's journey of realizing the value of family. Incorporate specific examples of how the character's attitude towards family changes throughout the narrative. Additionally, develop a moral to the story that emphasizes the significance of familial bonds.
output:
Lucas had always seen himself as independent and self-sufficient. He believed that he could handle anything on his own and that family was nothing more than just a group of people that share the same bloodline. However, as time went by, he started to realize that family is much more than that.

Growing up, Lucas had everything he could ask for, except for a close bond with his family. His parents, both lawyers, were always busy with work, and his older siblings were already off to college when he was still a kid. He spent most of his childhood in fancy boarding schools where he was taught to be independent and stand on his own two feet. He learned how to take care of himself, and he was proud of it.

When he was old enough, Lucas moved out of his parents' house and never looked back. He got a job as a marketing executive in a big corporation and quickly climbed the corporate ladder. Life was good, and he felt accomplished. But deep down inside, he felt like something was missing.

It wasn't until Lucas's parents got sick that he realized what he had been missing all along. Suddenly, he found himself surrounded by his family, all of whom had put their differences aside to come together to support their ailing parents. The love and camaraderie he saw among them were foreign to him. As he watched their daily visits and genuine concern for his parents' well-being, he couldn't help but feel out of place.

Lucas realized that his attitude towards family had been all wrong. He had always believed that family was just something that would always be there, but now he saw that he had taken his family's love and support for granted all along. It hit him hard when he realized that he had never reciprocated their love and support, and he was guilt-ridden.

One day, while he was sitting by his father's bedside, Lucas broke down in tears. He apologized to his parents for not being there for them, for not understanding the importance of family, and for being a selfish son all these years. It was then that Lucas decided to make amends.

Lucas started to spend more time with his family. He organized family dinners, movie nights, and even a weekend vacation. Lucas enjoyed getting to know his siblings and parents, and he cherished every moment he spent with them. He saw how much they loved him and how much they had missed him.

As he was driving home from a family gathering, Lucas realized that family is much more than just people who share the same DNA. Family is a bond that transcends time and place. It's an unbreakable connection that gives us love, support, and the foundation to build a life. Lucas had finally understood the significance of his family, and he was grateful for them.

In conclusion, the narrative about Lucas's journey to realizing the value of family emphasizes the significance of familial bonds. By narrating Lucas's experiences, the story depicts how his understanding of family was skewed by his past perceptions, and how life-changing events led him to see the true value of family. The story highlights the importance of family in our lives, and how our relationships with them shape our existence. The moral of the story is that family is an unbreakable bond that must be nurtured and cherished throughout our lives.

instruction:
It is quite common for teachers to request students to write an A view from the bridge essay. Since this is such a popular topic, this essay is not supposed to be shockingly original but solid, well-based on personal readings and logically sustained. However, there are some mistakes that students tend to make, not only when it comes to this famous play but with other literary essays as well.
A View from the Bridge is a play by American playwright Arthur Miller, which was staged for the first time on September 29, 1955, on Broadway. The two-act version of the play that today is more frequently represented appeared a year after that. It is a great play with many reminiscences of the Greek tragedy, and it is one of teachersвЂ™ favourite topic when it comes to write literature essays. It is a wonderful play, although we understand you donвЂ™t have time to read its 70 pages (or more, depending on the edition) and you may require someone else to write the essay for you.
Maybe you are running out of time to read the full play and you are thinking вЂњHow about renting one of its versions as a movie and then write from it my A View from the Bridge essay?вЂќ. In fact, A View from the Bridge has been adapted many times, also in television. The most famous version in French movie Vu du Pont (1962). But watching only the movie and not checking the facts can be risky. It is very easy to analyze a specific scene, only to realize later (too late) that is wasnвЂ™t Arthur MillerвЂ™s writing but a directorвЂ™s choice. So try to watch the movie only if you are planning to compare and contrast different versions, or to complete your reading notes.
In all A View from the Bridge essays, as well as in other literary essays, it is not recommended to fill paragraphs with a summary of the plot. The teacher has read the book (at least we may assume that), so have you, you donвЂ™t need to prove it by retelling the story. Go straight to the main point and discuss specific story details only when relevant to your topic of choice. Just provide some basic facts about the plot of the play, such as the setting (an Italian American neighborhood near the Brooklyn Bridge in the 1950s), the main characters (Italian American longshoreman Eddie Carbone; his wife, Beatrice; his niece, Catherine). Not much more.
Any A View from the Bridge essay should include quotations from literary criticism. For example, donвЂ™t forget to mention somewhere the comparison between Arthur MillerвЂ™s play and the Greek tragedy. It is true that you have to express your own ideas and thoughts, but quoting authorities is also important.

Provide some basic facts about the plot of the play, but not much more. The teacher has read the book, and so have you, so there is no need to prove it by retelling the story.

1. Research literary criticism on the play: Before you start writing your essay, do some research on what literary critics have said about A View from the Bridge. This will give you a better understanding of the play and help you develop your own ideas.

2. Use quotes from critics: When you incorporate literary criticism into your essay, be sure to use quotes from critics to support your own ideas. Use these quotes as evidence to support your argument.

3. Analyze different interpretations: Literary criticism often offers different interpretations of a text. Analyze these different interpretations to gain a deeper understanding of the play. Include your own opinion on which interpretation you think is most valid.

4. Avoid summarizing criticism: Just like you should avoid summarizing the plot of the play, avoid summarizing literary criticism. Instead, use it to develop your own point of view.

instruction:
PHOENIX – With a steady job in the federal government, the last thing one single mother in Phoenix expected to have to do to get by was sell her plasma.
But Jo Ann Goodlow, who works for the Bureau of Land Management, has sold plasma to keep her family afloat during the partial government shutdown.
She already has a part-time job and is about to start another one.
“I’m not sitting at home doing nothing,” the mother of three told KTAR News 92.3 FM’s Mac & Gaydos on Wednesday, the 26th day of furloughs for hundreds of thousands of federal employees.
Making ends meet still has been a struggle for Goodlow.
“You kind of put things off because you think … we’re going to be OK, but realistically, it wasn’t going to be OK,” she said.
Her last federal paycheck was issued over the holidays.
A week ago, Goodlow reluctantly set up a GoFundMe account.
“I didn’t want people to know. … I don’t ask for help from anybody because I do for myself.
So far givers have raised a little more than $16,000. Goodlow’s goal had been $5,000.
“It’s been so overwhelming. I’m very grateful,” she said.
The first flow of kindness came from the parents of her 17-year-old son’s teammates and friends at Pinnacle High.
Her son had been been having problems with his wisdom teeth. Other parents paid for the dental work.
The public appeal also has drawn blowback.
Commenters have questioned Goodlow’s motives in setting up the page.
“That part hurts. I haven’t even touched any of the money. The bills are just sitting here right now,” she said.
But besides her high schooler, Goodlow is also the breadwinner to a 6-year-old and a 4-year-old.
“We’ve cut back pretty much on everything. We don’t live lavishly,” she said.
Goodlow has asked that visitors to her online fundraiser consider donating to another family struggling through the shutdown.
Could you paraphrase some of the comments that have been made about Goodlow's GoFundMe page and how she has responded to them?
output: Commenters on Jo Ann Goodlow's GoFundMe page have questioned her motives in setting up the fundraiser. Goodlow has stated that it hurts her to receive criticism and that she hasn't touched any of the money raised. She has also asked visitors to her page to consider donating to other families struggling through the shutdown.

instruction: Can you please provide more information on how Jo Ann Goodlow's GoFundMe page has been received by the public? I'm interested to know if there has been any support or criticism for her decision.
output: There has been both support and criticism for Jo Ann Goodlow's GoFundMe page. Some individuals have been moved by her story and have generously donated to her cause, resulting in her exceeding her goal of $5,000 within a few days. Others have criticized her decision to ask for help and have questioned her motives. Goodlow has responded by acknowledging the criticism and expressing gratitude for the donations she has received. She has also asked visitors to her page to consider donating to other families struggling through the shutdown.

instruction: Create a visually appealing and easy-to-read guide that outlines the best healthy snack options available at a typical convenience store, including information on nutritional content, ingredients to avoid, and tips for making the healthiest choices possible. The guide should be accessible to people of all ages and dietary preferences, and should include a mix of pre-packaged snacks as well as fresh options like fruits and vegetables. Additionally, the guide should provide suggestions for managing portion sizes and avoiding overconsumption of sugar, salt, and other unhealthy ingredients commonly found in convenience store snacks.
output:
*Note: This guide includes some general healthy eating tips and is not meant to replace individualized nutritional recommendations from a healthcare professional. 

VISUAL GUIDE TO HEALTHY CONVENIENCE STORE SNACKS

When you're on-the-go or in a rush, a convenience store can have plenty of tempting but unhealthy snack options. However, with a little knowledge and planning, you can make choices that support your health and energy levels.

Tips for healthy snacking:
- Look for snacks that contain protein and fiber to keep you feeling full for longer.
- Read labels and avoid snacks with lots of added sugars, artificial ingredients, and unhealthy fats.
- Choose fresh fruits and vegetables when possible, and keep portion sizes in mind to avoid over-consuming.

1. Packaged snacks:
- KIND bars: These bars contain nuts, seeds, and natural sweeteners like honey for a satisfying snack with no artificial ingredients.
- RXBARs: These protein bars have a short list of easily recognizable ingredients, like egg whites, nuts, and fruits.
- Popcorn: Look for low-sodium and light varieties without added butter or flavorings.
- Jerky: Choose lean meats like turkey or salmon and avoid those with preservatives or added sugars.
- Veggie chips: Brands like Terra offer chips made from a variety of vegetables with minimal added oils and seasoning.
- Yogurt: Greek yogurt cups can provide protein and calcium, but watch out for added sugars and flavors. 

2. Fresh options:
- Fresh fruit: Depending on the season and location, most convenience stores should have at least some fresh produce options like apples, bananas, or grapes.
- Vegetables and hummus: Some stores may offer pre-packaged baby carrots or bell pepper slices with hummus for dipping. 
- Hard-boiled eggs: Protein-packed and easy to eat on-the-go. 
- Cheese sticks: A portion-controlled snack with protein and calcium. 
- Trail mix: Make your own with a mix of nuts, seeds, and a small portion of dried fruit. 
- Smoothies: Look for options made with whole fruit and natural sweeteners like honey, and watch out for portion sizes and added sugars.

Remember, even though these snacks may be healthier than other convenience store options, they can still be high in calories or salt if consumed in large amounts. Listen to your hunger cues and be mindful of serving sizes to make the most of your snack choices.

instruction: Develop a referral program for a makeup artist that incentivizes current clients to refer new clients. instruction:
Given the text: Boil onion for 5 minutes in salted water.
Strain, mix with rest of ingredients, binding with egg.
Loosen the flesh on the under side of joint, insert knife and make a ‘pocket’ for the stuffing.
Press some of the stuffing into this pocket, sew or skewer the ends together.
Make remainder of stuffing into balls, which may be cooked around the joint.
Unless the meat seems very lean, there is no need to add extra fat.
Allow 30 mins. Per lb. And 30 mins. Over, weigh the meat when it is stuffed.
Can you provide a recipe for a stuffed joint of meat?
output:
Ingredients:
- 1 joint of meat (pork, beef, lamb or veal)
- 1 onion
- 1 cup breadcrumbs
- 1 egg
- 1 tablespoon chopped fresh herbs (parsley, thyme, rosemary)
- Salt and pepper, to taste

Instructions:

1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Boil the onion in salted water for 5 minutes, then strain and chop it finely.

3. In a mixing bowl, combine the chopped onion with the breadcrumbs, egg, fresh herbs, and salt and pepper.

4. Loosen the flesh on the under side of the joint of meat with a knife, then insert the knife to create a ‘pocket’ for the stuffing.

5. Press some of the prepared stuffing into the pocket, then sew or skewer the ends together to secure the stuffing inside.

6. Form the remainder of the stuffing into small balls, which can be cooked around the joint of meat.

7. Place the joint of meat in a roasting pan, season with salt and pepper if desired, and roast for 30 minutes per pound plus an additional 30 minutes.

8. When the joint of meat is done, remove it from the oven and allow it to rest for 10 minutes before carving.

9. Serve the carved meat with the stuffing balls and your choice of sides. Enjoy!

instruction: Can you please suggest how I can modify this recipe for a vegetarian option using the same stuffing ingredients?
output:
Sure, here's a modification of the recipe for a vegetarian option:

Ingredients:
- 1 small butternut squash
- 1 onion
- 1 cup breadcrumbs
- 1 egg (optional, can be substituted with vegan egg replacer)
- 1 tablespoon chopped fresh herbs (parsley, thyme, rosemary)
- Salt and pepper, to taste
- Olive oil

Instructions:
1. Preheat the oven to 350°F.

2. Cut the butternut squash in half lengthwise and remove the seeds and fibers.

3. Brush the inside of each squash half with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.

4. Roast the squash halves in the preheated oven for 30 minutes, or until they are soft.

5. While the squash is roasting, boil the onion in salted water for 5 minutes, then strain and chop it finely.

6. In a mixing bowl, combine the chopped onion with the breadcrumbs, egg replacer (if using), fresh herbs, and salt and pepper.

7. Once the squash is cooked and cooled, carefully spoon out some of the flesh to create a ‘pocket’ for the stuffing.

8. Press some of the prepared stuffing into the pocket of each squash half.

9. Place the squash halves in a roasting pan, and bake them for 15-20 minutes, or until the stuffing is browned and crispy.

10. Serve the stuffed squash with your choice of sides. Enjoy!

instruction: Research the impact of film education on the industry.
output:
Film education has a significant impact on the industry in various ways. 

Firstly, film education provides a platform for aspiring filmmakers to learn and enhance their skills. Film schools offer courses in cinematography, directing, producing, screenwriting, acting, and post-production. These courses provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the technical aspects of filmmaking, storytelling, budgeting, and marketing. As a result, film education helps to nurture and develop new talent, which forms the backbone of the film industry.

Secondly, film education also helps to raise the quality of films produced. The knowledge and skills gained from these educational programs are often translated into better production, more coherent storytelling, and overall better quality films. This, in turn, increases the box office revenue of the film industry and makes it more profitable.

Thirdly, film education helps to preserve the history and culture of film. Film schools teach students about the art and history of filmmaking and encourage them to study the works of legendary directors and producers. This enhances the appreciation of classic films and promotes new ways of thinking about film. Film education, therefore, plays a crucial role in ensuring that the cultural significance of the industry is not lost.

Lastly, film education helps to create job opportunities in the industry by training individuals with the necessary skills and knowledge to work in various fields, such as production, distribution, and marketing. This not only benefits the individuals but also contributes to the growth and stability of the industry.

In summary, film education has a positive impact on the industry by nurturing new talent, improving the quality of films, preserving film history and culture, and creating job opportunities.

These are just a few examples of famous filmmakers who have benefited from film education.

instruction: Write a supernatural romance about a human falling deeply in love with a vampire, exploring the forbidden nature of their relationship and the challenges they face as they navigate their worlds of light and darkness. Consider how their different perspectives on immortality, death, and human frailty impact their growing intimacy, and infuse your story with elements of danger, ambiguity, and mystery to keep readers on the edge of their seats. Use lush, descriptive language to create a vivid sense of place, and lean into the atmospheric tension between human desire and vampiric impulses to craft a hauntingly beautiful love story.
output:
The night was dark, and the moon cast a pale glow over the city as Alice made her way home from work. She never felt safe walking alone at night, but tonight, she was feeling more nervous than usual. Something about the shadows seemed to follow her, and with each step she took, the feeling of being watched grew.

Suddenly, a figure stepped out from behind a building. It was a man, tall and lean with striking features that seemed to catch the moon's light. As he approached her, Alice's heart began to race. She wanted to bolt, but something about his presence kept her rooted to the spot.

"Are you lost?" he asked in a voice that was both smooth and deep.

Alice glanced around, realizing she had wandered into a part of town she didn't know very well. "No, I'm not lost," she said, her voice shaking slightly.

He took a step closer, and Alice could see the intricate patterns on his black coat. "It's not safe for you to be out here alone," he said. "Let me walk you home."

Alice hesitated for a moment, but the stranger had a calming presence about him that made her feel safe. They walked in silence, and Alice couldn't help but notice his eyes. They were a deep, piercing blue that seemed to see beyond the surface.

When they arrived at her doorstep, he turned to her and said, "My name is Alexander. Thank you for allowing me to walk you home."

"Thank you," Alice replied, feeling an unexpected touch of sadness as he turned to leave.

Over the days that followed, Alice couldn't shake the memory of Alexander from her mind. He seemed to have an uncanny ability to appear out of nowhere, and she found herself looking for him at every turn.

It wasn't until they ran into each other at the park that they truly connected. They found themselves sitting on a bench, talking for hours as if they had known each other their entire lives. Alice couldn't explain the pull she felt towards him. Every time his gaze drifted towards her, she felt as though he was seeing something in her that no one else ever had.

It wasn't until the sun began to set that Alexander stood up, saying he had to leave. Alice watched him go, feeling an odd sense of emptiness in his absence.

It wasn't until weeks later that Alice realized what set Alexander apart from other men. He was a vampire, cursed to walk the earth forever. But even when she learned the truth, it did not dull the intensity of their love.

As their relationship deepened, they realized the complexities of their love. Alexander lived in a world of darkness, and Alice lived in a world of light. They both had vastly different perspectives on life and death, and immortality weighed heavily on them both.

They were constantly faced with the obstacles of their worlds, with the danger of Alexander's thirst for blood ever-present. But together they braved the challenges, building a bond that was unbreakable.

Alice had never believed in the supernatural, but her love for Alexander had opened her eyes to a world of mystery and intrigue that she had never known existed. Together, they explored the boundaries between life and death, light and darkness, humanity and vampirism.

Their love was forbidden, but they could not deny their feelings for one another. As they roamed the dark city streets, Alice could not help but feel alive in ways she had never felt before. Their love was a hauntingly beautiful force that transcended the bounds of mortality.

As the years passed, Alice realized that although they were from different worlds, there was no force in the world that could keep them apart. They would remain forever entwined in a love that was both immortal and everlasting.

instruction: Write a step-by-step guide on how to set up and effectively use Trello for managing a project, including how to create boards, lists, and cards, assign tasks to team members, track progress, and collaborate efficiently. Provide tips on best practices for labeling, tagging, and organizing information within Trello, as well as suggestions for integrating other project management tools or software.
output:
Step-by-Step Guide on how to set up and effectively use Trello for managing a project:

1. Sign up for a Trello account: Go to the Trello website and sign up for an account with your email address.

2. Create a board: After signing up, create a board by clicking the (+) icon in the upper right corner of the Trello dashboard.  Name your board with a descriptive title relevant to your project. 

3. Create lists: A Trello board is made of lists. Create a list to represent each stage of your project such as "To Do", "In Progress", "Complete", etc.

4. Add cards: Each card represents a task in your project. Click "Add a card" to create a card for each task in your "To Do" list. Add as much detail as you can, and use the comment section to add further notes.

5. Assign tasks to team members: Click on the card to open it, and you'll be able to assign the task to yourself or any member of your team.

6. Track progress: As tasks are completed move them to the "Completed" list. Use labels [board filters] to identify priority, type of task or to add more information about the task.

7. Collaborate efficiently: Enable commenting on the board and on each card.  Members can make comments on the progress of a task, and manage text communication within the tool.

8. Best Practices:

Labeling- Labels aren’t just useful for marking progress. They can also be used to denote different types of tasks, assign priority, or even identify which team member is responsible for the task.

Tagging: Using tags like #design, #development or #marketing for different types of tasks, will aid in quickly defining what's been done and what needs to be done.

Organization: Use the "Custom Fields" and "Power-Ups" options in the Trello menu to add more details about tasks and team members.

Integration with other software: Trello offers a lot of integrations that can work seamlessly together. Try to use it with software like G-Suite, Slack, IFTTT for a more efficient workflow.

Implementing these best practices can help to simplify complex projects, streamline team communication, and ensure successful project completion.

instruction: Thanks for the step-by-step guide on how to use Trello for managing a project. Can you please add more information on how to use the calendar view in Trello and how to integrate it with other productivity tools like Google Calendar?
output:
Yes, absolutely! Here's more information on using the calendar view in Trello and integrating it with other productivity tools:

Using the calendar view in Trello:
Trello has a calendar view that can be very helpful in managing your projects. Here is how to access and use the Trello calendar view:

1. Open your Trello project board and click the “Show Menu” button.

2. From the menu, select “Power-Ups”, then search for “Calendar” and enable it.

3. Once the Calendar Power-Up is enabled, you will see a new “Calendar” option in the menu. Click on “Calendar” to see a calendar view of all the cards on your board.

4. You can also filter cards by labels and assign due dates to cards so that they show up on specific dates.

5. Drag and drop cards on the calendar to schedule and reschedule tasks as needed.

Integrating Trello with Google Calendar:
You can also integrate Trello with Google Calendar to help you stay on top of your deadlines and easily manage your schedule.

1. To integrate Trello and Google Calendar, open your Trello account and click on the three dots in the top right corner of the calendar.

2. From the drop-down menu, select “Calendar Feed” and copy the link provided.

3. Open your Google Calendar and click the “+” icon next to “Other calendars” on the left-hand panel.

4. From the drop-down menu, select “From URL”.

5. Paste the Trello Calendar Feed link into the URL field and click “Add Calendar.”

6. Now all of the due dates from your Trello board will be displayed on your Google Calendar.

By following these steps, you can integrate Trello and Google Calendar to have a comprehensive view of all your deadlines in one place.

instruction: How has the history of Athens, Greece influenced its current cultural identity?
output:
The history of Athens, Greece has had a significant influence on its current cultural identity in the following ways:

1. Democracy: Athens is considered the birthplace of democracy, where citizens participated in the decision-making process of the government. This concept of democracy has influenced the country's governance even after centuries, and the Greek Parliament still reflects a democratic structure.

2. Philosophy and education: Athens was home to famous philosophers like Socrates, Plato, and Aristotle, whose teachings have had a profound impact on Western philosophy. The city is also recognized for its world-renowned academic institutions like the Athens University of Economics and Business, the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens, which have produced many prominent thinkers, scientists, and philosophers.

3. Architecture and arts: Greek architecture and arts are recognized worldwide, and Athens has some noteworthy artifacts like the ancient Acropolis, the Parthenon, and the Temple of Olympian Zeus, which remain accessible and well preserved. The city has also produced famous artists like El Greco and Yannis Moralis, whose works have enriched the country's cultural heritage.

4. Sports: Athens is the originator of the Olympic Games that have become an international phenomenon. The games have been an emblem of athleticism and sportsmanship, with the city hosting the Olympics twice, in 1896 and 2004.

Therefore, the history of Athens, Greece has significantly influenced its current cultural identity and has made it a vital contributor to the world's civilizations.

instruction: I've heard that Athens is also known for its delicious cuisine. How has the city's history influenced the local food culture?
output:
Yes, Athens is well-known for its delicious cuisine, which has been influenced by its history and cultural heritage. Here are some ways that the city's history has influenced its food culture:

1. Historical trade routes: Athens has a rich culinary heritage traced back to the ancient world, with recipes and ingredients from various civilizations that once passed through the city, including the Ottoman Empire, Venetian, Persian, and Byzantine empires. The ingredients and spices used in Athens' food culture reflect this diverse cultural past.

2. Agricultural traditions: Athens has a long history of agriculture, and the fertile land surrounding the city has contributed to its food culture. The traditional dishes often include local produce like olives, feta cheese, honey, and seafood as the city is close to the sea.

3. Religion: The Eastern Orthodox Church has a significant influence on Athens' food culture, with many dishes prepared during religious festivals and periods. For example, during the Lent period, people consume lentils, and on Easter, they prepare lamb dishes.

4. Ruling empires: Athens has been ruled by several empires throughout its history, and each has left its mark on the city's food culture. For example, dishes like moussaka and dolmades have been influenced by Ottoman Empire cuisine.

In conclusion, Athens' history has influenced its local food culture by bringing together diverse ingredients and cooking styles, emphasizing local agriculture and produce, and creating traditional dishes from its historical past.

Can you provide a recipe for a vegetable puree with zucchini and spinach, and how to serve it with halibut?: This dish looks especially pretty if plated like this: make a thin circle of the zucchini puree on a plate. Stack eggplant and onion on top of zucchini paste circle. Place halibut on top of the onions; drizzle fish with basil puree; and garnish with roasted pepper and tomato salad and a fried basil leaf.
Zucchini Puree: Cut green zucchini away from the center and dice. Triple blanch peeled garlic by boiling in water, then shocking in cold water and repeating this process 2 more times. Set aside. In a medium pan, add olive oil and zucchini, allowing time for zucchini to sweat. Then, add chicken stock, cover, and let simmer for 15 to 20 minutes. Add triple blanched garlic and cream, cook further for 5 minutes. Blend in a blender, adding fresh spinach. Strain into a bowl resting in an ice bath and let cool immediately.
Basil Puree: Place egg yolk with rice wine vinegar and basil in a blender. Blend adding grapeseed oil slowly until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Eggplant and Onions: Mix the honey with the thyme and let stand 30 minutes. Slice eggplant about 1 to 1 1/2 inches thick. Rinse and dry. Sear on flat grill on both sides. Brush with thyme infused honey and bake in the oven for 10 to 15 minutes. Slice onion about 1/2-inch thick. Sear on the grill, then roast in preheated 375-degree oven for 10 minutes.
output:
Roasted Pepper and Tomato Salad: Cut a red pepper and 2 tomatoes into small pieces. Drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper. Roast in 375-degree oven for 20 minutes, or until veggies are tender.

To serve: Spread a thin circle of zucchini puree on a plate. Stack eggplant and onion on top of zucchini paste circle. Place halibut on top of the onions; drizzle fish with basil puree; and garnish with roasted pepper and tomato salad and a fried basil leaf. Enjoy!

instruction: Please provide an example of a specific machine learning algorithm that has been successfully applied to predictive maintenance in the manufacturing industry. Include details about the data sources used, the types of predictive models developed, any challenges encountered, and the overall impact on maintenance efficiency and cost savings.
output:
One specific machine learning algorithm that has been successfully applied to predictive maintenance in the manufacturing industry is the Random Forest algorithm. 

In a case study carried out by SKF, a leading bearing and rotating equipment technology company, Random Forest algorithm was used to predict maintenance needs in wind turbines. The data sources used included vibration data collected using sensors installed in the wind turbine gearbox, generator, and bearing components. The data set also included weather data that was collected from local weather stations to help determine the relationship between temperature and wind speed with the system's performance. 

The Random Forest algorithm was used to develop predictive models that could identify specific defects in the wind turbines, including bearing damages, gear failures, and misalignments. The algorithm's high accuracy in detecting anomalies and abnormalities that are difficult to find using traditional techniques helped the company to carry out proactive maintenance and repair, avoiding costly downtime in production. 

One of the significant challenges encountered in implementing the system was the need for a large amount of data. The data had to be collected over an extended period, and the data quality had to be consistently high over time. Additionally, the models developed had to be continually updated, given the dynamic nature of the operating environment.

The overall impact of implementing the Random Forest algorithm was significant cost savings for the company, achieved through a reduction in reactive maintenance costs and increased asset uptime. SKF reported a 20% reduction in maintenance costs, extended maintenance cycles, and increased machine availability, leading to increased production efficiency.

instruction: This is great, but can you provide more details about how the Random Forest algorithm was trained to detect specific defects in wind turbines? Also, were there any other types of data sources used besides the vibration and weather data?
output:
Sure. To train the Random Forest algorithm to detect specific defects in wind turbines, SKF used a combination of supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques. This involved feeding the algorithm with labeled data (data with known defect types) and allowing it to learn from the patterns in the data to accurately predict the label of new, previously unseen observations. The algorithm was trained on features extracted from the vibration and temperature data, including signal amplitude, frequency, time-domain and spectral features.

To identify new defects that had not been previously observed, unsupervised learning techniques were used to detect anomalies in vibration and temperature data. This was done by finding patterns that deviated from normal operating trends in the absence of known defects, which would indicate the presence of potential issues.

Besides the vibration and weather data, SKF also used maintenance logs and operator reports to improve the accuracy of the Random Forest algorithm. This additional data was used to supplement the labeled training data set and to help the algorithm learn more about the operating and maintenance history of the wind turbines.

Overall, the combination of labeled and unlabeled data sources, along with a variety of machine learning techniques, allowed SKF to develop a highly accurate predictive maintenance system that could detect specific defects in wind turbines and identify new anomalies that could not be detected by traditional methods.

As I covered last week, most people who have a website for marketing their business have one of three problems with it.
The website is producing no leads or sales and they have no idea what to do, or whether anyone is even coming to the site.
The website is producing a few leads or sales, but the owner doesn’t know how to increase it.
The website is producing a decent flow of leads or sales, and the website owner wants to increase that, but doesn’t know how.
Last week I covered PPC and organic traffic. In this article I’ll cover blogs and next week social media.
Most people don’t realize that blogging is a powerful tool for driving traffic to a web site.
A blog is a special type of web site that makes it easy for you to add new content on a regular basis. New content gets added at the top, and you scroll down to see the older content.
WordPress is one of the most common blogging systems, allowing you to put up a blog within your web site, as a subfolder (http://www.yourwebsite.com/blog). Typepad is another common blogging system, allowing you to either having it set up under Typepad’s URL (http://yourblogname.typepad.com) or you can set up a separate web address for the blog (http://www.yourblogname.com).
There are also several free blogging sites, where you can set up a blog, such as Blogger.com and Tumblr.com, and then your blog URL is something like http://yourblogname.blogspot.com or http://yourblogname.tumblr.com. But these sites are much more limited in the features and design templates you can use. It’s much harder to customize the blog to your needs than with WordPress or Typepad.
Blog design: When setting up a blog it is vital to design it with one or two sidebars, then add your contact information, and several links to features on your main web site. For example you could link to your home page, your “about us” page, your services page, and so on. If you sell any items such as books you can put an ad for the book in one of the sidebars. You want to set up the blog in such a way that as many people as possible who come to the blog also go over to your web site.
Now, you should put new content up on your blog regularly. By regularly, ideally I mean once a week or more often. Content can be anything from a long article (700-1,000 words), to a press release, to a shorter post or comment about something related to the topic of your blog (100-200 words).
In the case of blogs there are over 20 search engines that are geared just to blogs. If you notify them, with what is called a “ping,” those search engines will all stop by your blog immediately and include your new article or other post in their search engine listings. There is a site called www.pingomatic.com that allows you to easily send a ping to 22 of these search engines.
This means that if your article was about how to lower your golf score, and someone went to one of these blog search engines and typed in “how to lower your golf score,” and your article contained that phrase, your listing would come up, allowing that person to click through and come to your blog.
I have two blogs for my marketing business, one for articles and a separate one for press releases. I post something to one of the two blogs a minimum of once a week. And I always send a ping to all of the blog search engines after every single post.
For the entire year of 2010 up to today, my two blogs have generated more traffic to my main web site, than any other source. In fact, if you add them up, it is three times the traffic that I got from Google.
So blogging can be a very powerful way to drive traffic to your web site.

instruction: Thank you for the detailed overview of the evolution of calligraphy. I found it fascinating how calligraphy has been used in different contexts, from religious to secular settings. Could you please add more information about the impact of calligraphy on contemporary art and design? Also, how has technology influenced the practice of calligraphy?
output:
Certainly! Calligraphy has had a significant impact on contemporary art and design, especially in the fields of typography and graphic design. Calligraphy's emphasis on form, balance, and harmony can be seen in many contemporary fonts, logos, and designs.

Calligraphic scripts have been used as inspirations for many contemporary typefaces, with designers aiming to capture the elegance and expressiveness of the calligraphic tradition. For example, the brush script, which is inspired by the Chinese running style script, has been widely used in advertising, branding, and packaging.

Moreover, calligraphy has also been used as an expression of individual and cultural identity in contemporary art. Many artists have embraced calligraphy as a way of exploring their identity, culture, and aesthetics. Calligraphy has become a medium for artistic expression that transcends cultural and linguistic boundaries.

Furthermore, technology has brought significant changes to the practice of calligraphy. Digital tools, such as tablets and stylus pens, have made it easier and faster for calligraphers to create their work. Digital tools also enable calligraphers to experiment with new techniques and styles, incorporating a wider range of materials and media.

However, some calligraphers argue that technology has both positive and negative consequences for the practice of calligraphy. On the one hand, digital tools have made it easier to master the basic techniques of calligraphy. On the other hand, some believe that the tactile experience of creating calligraphy with traditional materials, such as paper and ink, cannot be replicated with digital tools.

In conclusion, calligraphy has had a profound impact on contemporary art and design. It has influenced typography and graphics, and has become a medium for artistic expression that transcends cultural and linguistic boundaries. Furthermore, technology has brought significant changes to the practice of calligraphy, both positive and negative, enabling artists to experiment with new techniques and materials.

instruction: Thank you for the insightful information on the influence of calligraphy on contemporary art and design. Could you please provide more information about the cultural significance of calligraphy in non-Asian cultures? How has calligraphy been received and interpreted in different parts of the world?
output:
Certainly. Calligraphy, which originated in East Asia, has had a significant influence on non-Asian cultures as well. It has been received and integrated differently in different parts of the world, leading to unique expressions and styles of calligraphy.

In the Islamic world, calligraphy has a rich history and continues to play an important role in cultural expression. Calligraphy is considered a sacred art form and has a deep connection to the Islamic faith. The Quran, the holy book of Islam, is written in classical Arabic calligraphy, and the art form is used to decorate mosques, religious texts, and other objects. Islamic calligraphy has also been used to inscribe poetry and other literature, and has found a place in architecture, textiles, and other artistic forms.

In Europe, calligraphy was originally associated with the scriptoria and the monastic tradition. Monks were responsible for copying religious texts, manuscripts, and illuminated books in the Middle Ages, and calligraphy was regarded as a critical skill. Over time, calligraphy became associated with more secular forms of art, such as painting, and has influenced typography, graphic design, and logo design.

In America, calligraphy has had a longstanding tradition, rooted in the country's manuscript history. Many important documents and manuscripts, such as the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution, were written in beautiful calligraphic scripts. Today, calligraphy plays an essential role in both the artistic and the commercial domains in America.

In Africa, calligraphy has developed a distinct aesthetic, influenced by indigenous handwriting styles and calligraphic traditions from the Arabic and Islamic world. Calligraphy is used to express various aspects of African identity, culture, and history. The Nsibidi script in Nigeria, for example, is a calligraphic form of writing used by the Ekpe society for secret communication.

In India, calligraphy has a rich history, with many distinct regional styles of writing. Calligraphy was used to record religious texts and epic poetry, and it was believed that the act of writing had spiritual benefits. Today, calligraphy is used for artistic expression, such as in the tradition of miniature painting.

In conclusion, calligraphy has been received and interpreted differently in various parts of the world, leading to distinctive styles and expressions. While calligraphy originated in East Asia, it has found its place in many cultural traditions and has been used for artistic and religious expression across the globe. Calligraphy's cultural significance lies in its ability to bridge linguistic and cultural boundaries and serve as a means of communication and artistic expression for people from diverse backgrounds.

instruction:
Can you recommend a dessert recipe that features cranberries, and what are some variations of this recipe?
Generate according to: Thanksgiving is not really a day for moderation. Once you’ve made it through the turkey, dressing, potatoes, sides, fresh vegetable or two, and whatever it is that makes your family meal uniquely yours, dessert awaits. But which dessert(s) will you bring to the table?
Our recipe collection has seen the addition of many holiday-worthy desserts over the years. To save you the trouble of scrolling through the more than 70 options in our archives, we’ve pulled out five of the best, and offered a few alternatives along the way. Because who has time to sift through all the Thanksgiving content you’re being bombarded with? We’ve done the sifting for you.
Fluffy Pumpkin Buttermilk Pie, above. This is not your average pumpkin pie. The gingersnap crust caramelizes and provides a crunchy texture boost, while the filling is light and fluffy thanks to whipped egg whites. We make a bit of a fuss about the variety of cinnamon you use here, but if that’s an obstacle to making this pie, you have our permission to ignore our advice; just know that a stronger-tasting cinnamon will mean a less subtly spiced pie. Also know that the crust works well with gluten-free gingersnaps.
Other pumpkin ideas: Vegan Pumpkin Pie With Coconut Cream (with molasses and pureed pecans!); Pumpkin-Caramel Tart With Toasted Hazelnut Crust (featuring a short bake time and a press-in crust); Maple and Pumpkin Custard (made in a cast-iron skillet, meaning it’s ideal for crust-phobes); Pumpkin Hazelnut Bars (easier to transport than a pie).
Albemarle Pippin Apple Cobbler. We don’t want to raise your expectations too much, but someone on our team has made this cobbler three times in the past few weeks. (Spoiler: That someone may be the author of this piece.) That’s a ringing endorsement if we’ve ever heard one! Seeking out this particular apple variety is all well and good, but if you can’t find it, please do try this with another tart apple, such as Winesap, Granny Smith, Empire, Cortland, Liberty and Jonathan.
More apples: Tiffany MacIsaac’s Double-Crust Apple Pie (classic!); Apple Gingerbread Cake (one-bowl, mix-by-hand); Turkey-Shaped Apple Tarts (fun to make with kids).
Tiny Tim Cranberry Tarts. This only works in a mini-muffin tin, and you must be sure to use no more than three cranberries per tart. Your reward for such strict adherence to the rules is two-bite tarts with a cream cheese pastry, a crunchy topping and the sweet-tart pop of berries inside.
More cranberries: Cranberry Apple Lattice Pie (with a red-wine-and-cranberry compote); Apple Cranberry Brown Betty (a lighter take on a classic); Cranberry Tart With Hazelnut Crust (guaranteed to be the showstopper on your dessert table).
Bourbon Pecan Pie. Featuring a higher-than-normal nut-to-filling ratio (meaning less goop, more crunch). The filling is sweetened with maple syrup and brown sugar, rather than corn syrup, and gets a pleasant kick from half a cup of bourbon. This also happens to be vegan.
Pecans elsewhere: Date Pecan Pie (best served cold); Pecangipane Pear and Cranberry Tart (looks fancy, freezes well).
Roasted Gingery Pears. This super-easy and infinitely flexible recipe from Julia Turshen can be made to accommodate nearly any diet. Gussy them up with maple-sweetened whipped cream, serve leftovers with yogurt the next day, and/or mash them up and turn them into a rustic sauce.
Patti LaBelle’s Sweet Potato Pie. Some may say that pumpkin and sweet potato pies are basically the same thing, but some people may also be wrong. Sweet potatoes lend more flavor, and this pie — you may recall it from its video fame? — has more nutmeg than you might be used to. Go with it; it works.
More sweet potatoes: Sweet Potato Cookies With Maple Glaze (soft and caky, more savory than sweet); Brown Sugar-Sweet Potato Cake (dense and moist); Persian-Spiced Sweet Potato Pie (no precooking of sweet potatoes required).
output:
For a dessert featuring cranberries, we recommend Cranberry Upside-Down Cake. To make this recipe, you'll need:

- 1 1/2 cups fresh cranberries
- 1/2 cup unsalted butter
- 1 cup brown sugar
- 2 eggs
- 1 3/4 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 teaspoons baking powder
- 1/4 teaspoon baking soda
- 1/4 teaspoon salt
- 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
- 1 cup buttermilk

To make the cranberry topping, melt 1/4 cup of the butter in a cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Add the brown sugar and stir to combine. Spread the cranberries evenly over the sugar mixture.

In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. In another bowl, cream the remaining butter with the vanilla and remaining brown sugar. Beat in the eggs, one at a time, then add the flour mixture in three batches, alternating with the buttermilk.

Pour the cake batter over the cranberries and smooth the top with a spatula. Bake in a 350-degree oven for about 40 minutes, or until the cake is golden brown and a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.

Variations on this recipe could include adding spices like cinnamon, nutmeg or ginger to the batter, or substituting some of the buttermilk with yogurt for extra tang. You could also try adding chopped nuts like pecans or almonds to the cranberry topping, or incorporating orange zest into the batter for a citrusy twist. Finally, instead of baking the cake in a skillet, you could try using a baking dish or individual ramekins for individual servings. Enjoy!

instruction: Can you suggest a variation for the Albemarle Pippin Apple Cobbler recipe? Something to spice it up a bit?
output:
Of course! To spice up the Albemarle Pippin Apple Cobbler recipe, try adding some warm spices like cinnamon, nutmeg, and ginger to the filling. You could also sprinkle some cardamom or allspice on top of the cobbler before baking for extra flavor.

Another option would be to add some diced crystallized ginger to the cobbler filling for a sweet and spicy kick. Or, you could try mixing in some dried cranberries or raisins for a chewy, fruity addition.

For a more boozy twist, try adding a splash of bourbon or rum to the filling, or deglazing the pan with some apple cider or hard cider before adding the apples.

Finally, you could experiment with different toppings for the cobbler, like a pecan streusel, a brown sugar and oat crumble, or a simple cinnamon sugar biscuit topping. All of these variations will add some extra excitement to the classic apple cobbler recipe. Enjoy!

instruction: What is the best irrigation method for tomato plants grown in sandy soil?
output: Drip irrigation is the best method for tomato plants grown in sandy soil. This method delivers water directly to the plant's root zone, reducing water loss through evaporation and ensuring that the plants receive a consistent supply of water. Additionally, drip irrigation can be coupled with fertilizer injection, allowing for precise nutrient delivery to the plants.

instruction: Can't I just water my tomato plants manually? It seems like it would be simpler than installing a drip irrigation system.
output: I do not have a preference, but I can provide you with information. While it is possible to water tomato plants manually, it can be challenging to provide them with consistent moisture levels, especially in sandy soil. Sandy soil doesn't hold moisture very well, which means it dries out quickly, and the plants' roots may not receive enough water. By using drip irrigation, you can better regulate moisture levels, ensuring that your tomato plants receive the right amount of water when they need it. This can lead to healthier plants and ultimately, a more abundant harvest.

instruction: What ingredients are needed and what is the step-by-step process for making homemade pizza sauce? Would you recommend a chunky or smooth texture for the sauce? Should we use fresh or canned tomatoes? Any tips for enhancing the flavor of the sauce?
output:
Ingredients:
- 1 can (28 oz) of whole peeled tomatoes
- 1 tablespoon tomato paste
- 2 garlic cloves, minced
- 1 teaspoon dried oregano
- 1 teaspoon dried basil
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1/2 teaspoon sugar
- 2 tablespoons olive oil

Steps:
1. Begin by adding the can of tomatoes to a blender and blending until smooth.
2. Heat olive oil in a saucepan and add minced garlic. Cook until fragrant.
3. Add tomato paste to the saucepan and cook for a few minutes, stirring constantly.
4. Add the blended tomatoes, oregano, basil, salt, pepper, and sugar to the saucepan.
5. Cook on low heat, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes or until the sauce has thickened.
6. Taste and adjust seasoning as necessary.
7. Once the sauce has cooled, store it in a jar or container in the refrigerator. It will keep for up to a week.

As for texture, it depends on personal preference. Some people prefer a smooth sauce while others like it chunky. This recipe creates a smooth sauce, but if you prefer it chunky, you can pulse the blended tomatoes in the blender a few times before adding them to the saucepan.

Using fresh tomatoes will result in a fresher taste, but canned tomatoes can be just as good if you use high-quality ones. Some tips for enhancing the flavor of the sauce include adding a pinch of red pepper flakes for spice, using fresh herbs instead of dried, or adding a teaspoon of balsamic vinegar for acidity.

instruction: Thank you for the recipe and instructions, but could you please provide more information on how to adjust the seasoning? Should I add more herbs or maybe some additional spices to make the sauce more flavorful? Also, is it possible to make the sauce spicier without making it too hot?
output:
To adjust the seasoning, you can taste the sauce and add more salt or pepper if you feel it needs it. If you want to add more flavor, you could consider adding more herbs such as fresh basil or oregano or even trying different spices like paprika or fennel seeds. You can also add a tablespoon of red wine or balsamic vinegar to add some depth and acidity to the sauce.

To make the sauce spicier without making it too hot, you can add a small amount of red pepper flakes or cayenne pepper, tasting as you go to make sure it's not too spicy. You could also consider adding a pinch of smoked paprika to add a smoky flavor without adding too much heat. Remember that a little bit of heat goes a long way, so start with a small amount and adjust as needed based on your preferences.

instruction:
Karine Joly is executive director of Higher Ed Experts, a professional development company, and editor of collegewebeditor.com.
Last week, Kyle James reminded us that the Center for Marketing Research at the University of Massachussets Dartmouth had just published the results of its latest study on social media use in higher ed.
With 456 interviews performed from November 2010 to May 2011 among a representative sample of 4-year institutions in the United States, the findings of this study are valid within a +/- 4 percent range.
While they confirm some widely-shared assumptions on the state of social media in higher education, these results also reveal some surprising trends.
According to this study, 100 percent of colleges and universities now use some form of social media–be it blogs, Facebook, Twitter, message/bulleting boards, videoblogging, podcasting, Foursquare, MySpace, LinkedIn or YouTube. Unsurprisingly, Facebook is the most widely used by institutions–only 2 percent aren’t present on the most popular social networking platform.
YouTube follows with an adoption rate of 86 percent, just before Twitter with 84 percent and blogging with 66 percent.
Is success in the eyes of the admissions officer?
When asked how successful institutions are with the different types of social media channels they use, more than three-quarters of the respondents reported all channels (with the exception of the dying MySpace platform) as successful.
So, all is for the best in the best of all possible worlds when it comes to social media in higher education?
A closer look at the results of two other recent studies, namely the 2011 E-expectations Study from Noel-Levitz and the State of Web and Social Media Analytics in Higher Education I conducted for Higher Ed Experts, raises several questions about the very rosy picture painted by the study of social media use in admissions offices.
When only 9 percent of prospective students and 5 percent of their parents have a Twitter account, according to the Noel-Levitz survey, how can 72 percent of the institutions see Twitter as a successful channel?
When 66 percent (a 15-point increase from the previous year) of admissions offices use blogs and three-quarters of students and parents said they never or only rarely looked at college blogs, how good can the social media strategy of the admission office be?
When 95 percent of admissions offices pat themselves on the back when asked to evaluate the success of their efforts on Facebook yet only 49 percent of the institutions–according to the Higher Ed Experts study–track Facebook activity, what does Facebook success look like for almost half the institutions?
Obviously, I don’t have the answers to these questions, but I believe there’s a real need to go beyond the “social media checklist” tactic and adopt a more strategic and measurable approach in higher education.
Now that everybody is on board, it’s time to find out what works for the institution and stop what doesn’t.
← Ask The Experts: What Do Alumni Want?
The college I intern for is still feeling it way through the dark. The FB and twitter are used to update followers(mostly alumni and a few faculty members) about campus news. The Facebook ads we ran had a decent CTR, but never converted. A lot of the stuff we do is attempting to build brand awareness and brand perceptions and perhaps promote alumni to tell (influence) prospective students to consider the college.
Based on the results of recent surveys, what questions are raised about the success and effectiveness of social media strategies used by admissions offices in higher education?
output: Recent surveys have raised questions about the success and effectiveness of social media strategies used by admissions offices in higher education. While 100% of colleges and universities use some form of social media, only 72% of institutions see Twitter as a successful channel, even though only 9% of prospective students and 5% of their parents have Twitter accounts. Additionally, while 66% of admissions offices use blogs, three-quarters of students and parents said they never or rarely look at college blogs, raising questions about the effectiveness of the social media strategy. Finally, while 95% of admissions offices consider their efforts on Facebook successful, only 49% of institutions track Facebook activity, leaving unclear what Facebook success looks like for almost half of the institutions. These findings suggest a need for institutions to adopt a more strategic and measurable approach to social media in higher education.

instruction: Can you provide any recommendations on how admissions offices can adopt a more strategic and measurable approach to social media in higher education?
output:
Sure, here are some recommendations for admissions offices to adopt a more strategic and measurable approach to social media in higher education:

1. Define measurable goals and KPIs: Admissions offices should clearly define their goals and key performance indicators (KPIs) for each social media channel they use. This will help them track the success of their social media efforts and make data-driven decisions.

2. Use data to inform social media strategy: Admissions offices should use data to understand their target audience, what social media channels they use, and what content they engage with the most. This will help them tailor their social media strategy to meet the needs and preferences of their audience.

3. Experiment with different types of content: Admissions offices should experiment with different types of content, such as video, images, or infographics, to see what resonates with their audience. They should also be open to trying new social media channels if they think it will help them reach their goals.

4. Invest in social media analytics tools: Admissions offices should invest in social media analytics tools to track their social media performance and get insights into what’s working and what’s not. This will help them optimize their social media strategy over time.

5. Collaborate with other departments: Admissions offices should collaborate with other departments, such as marketing or alumni relations, to create a cohesive social media strategy that supports the overall goals of the institution.

By adopting these recommendations, admissions offices can take a more strategic and measurable approach to social media in higher education, and ensure that they are reaching their target audience effectively.
