Explain how the brain-to-brain connection experiment is being expanded to help those with developmental impairment, stroke or ADHD. Answer according to: Researchers recently used a direct brain-to-brain connection to let pairs of people play a question-and-answer game by transmitting signals from one brain to the other over the internet.
The experiment, reported in PLOS ONE, may be the first to show that scientists can directly link two brains to allow one person to guess what’s on another person’s mind.
“This is the most complex brain-to-brain experiment, I think, that’s been done to date in humans,” says lead author Andrea Stocco, an assistant professor of psychology and a researcher at University of Washington’s Institute for Learning & Brain Sciences.
“It uses conscious experiences through signals that are experienced visually, and it requires two people to collaborate,” Stocco says.
The first participant, or “respondent,” wears a cap connected to an electroencephalography (EEG) machine that records electrical brain activity. The respondent is shown an object (for example, a dog) on a computer screen, and the second participant, or “inquirer,” sees a list of possible objects and associated questions.
With the click of a mouse, the inquirer sends a question and the respondent answers “yes” or “no” by focusing on one of two flashing LED lights attached to the monitor, which flash at different frequencies.
The phosphene—which might look like a blob, waves, or a thin line—is created through a brief disruption in the visual field and tells the inquirer the answer is yes. Through answers to these simple yes or no questions, the inquirer identifies the correct item.
The experiment was carried out in dark rooms in two labs located almost a mile apart and involved five pairs of participants, who played 20 rounds of the question-and-answer game. Each game had eight objects and three questions that would solve the game if answered correctly. The sessions were a random mixture of 10 real games and 10 control games that were structured the same way.
“We took many steps to make sure that people were not cheating,” Stocco says.
What is your brain seeing?
“While the flashing lights are signals that we’re putting into the brain, those parts of the brain are doing a million other things at any given time too,” Prat says.
The study builds on the team’s initial experiment in 2013, when it was the first to demonstrate a direct brain-to-brain connection between humans. Other scientists have connected the brains of rats and monkeys, and transmitted brain signals from a human to a rat, using electrodes inserted into animals’ brains. In the 2013 experiment, the team used noninvasive technology to send a person’s brain signals over the Internet to control the hand motions of another person.
The first experiment evolved out of research by coauthor Rajesh Rao, a professor of computer science and engineering, on brain-computer interfaces that enable people to activate devices with their minds. In 2011, Rao began collaborating with Stocco and Prat to determine how to link two human brains together.
In 2014, the researchers received a grant from the W.M. Keck Foundation that allowed them to broaden their experiments to decode more complex interactions and brain processes. They are now exploring the possibility of “brain tutoring,” transferring signals directly from healthy brains to ones that are developmentally impaired or impacted by external factors such as a stroke or accident, or simply to transfer knowledge from teacher to pupil.
The team is also working on transmitting brain states—for example, sending signals from an alert person to a sleepy one, or from a focused student to one who has attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, or ADHD.
Many technological advancements over the past century, from the telegraph to the internet, were created to facilitate communication between people. The team’s work takes a different approach, using technology to strip away the need for such intermediaries.
“Evolution has spent a colossal amount of time to find ways for us and other animals to take information out of our brains and communicate it to other animals in the forms of behavior, speech, and so on,” Stocco says. “But it requires a translation. We can only communicate part of whatever our brain processes.
“What we are doing is kind of reversing the process a step at a time by opening up this box and taking signals from the brain and with minimal translation, putting them back in another person’s brain,” he says.

instruction: Compare and contrast the use of imagery, tone, and structure in two poems with similar themes. Analyze the differences and similarities in the way each poet conveys the theme through their poetic devices. Give specific examples from both poems to support your claims.
output:
Two poems with similar themes that use imagery, tone, and structure differently are "The Waste Land" by T.S. Eliot and "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" also by T.S. Eliot. Both poems explore the theme of disillusionment and the fragmentation of modern life, but they convey these ideas through different poetic devices.

In "The Waste Land," Eliot uses vivid and complex imagery to create a bleak and desolate landscape. The poem is divided into five sections, each with its own distinct imagery and tone. In the first section, "The Burial of the Dead," Eliot uses a variety of images to convey the decay and decay of modern society. For example, he describes "the dead tree gives no shelter, the cricket no relief" and "the river's tent is shattered by the siege of winter." These images create a sense of hopelessness and despair that runs throughout the poem.

In contrast, "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" uses more subtle and understated imagery. The poem is structured as a series of fragmented and disjointed thoughts, with Prufrock's inner monologue creating a sense of confusion and uncertainty. The poem's tone is introspective and melancholy, conveying a sense of isolation and disillusionment. For example, Prufrock describes himself as "an attendant lord, one that will do / To swell a progress, start a scene or two / Advise the prince; no doubt, an easy tool." These images create a sense of ennui and apathy that is a recurring theme throughout the poem.

Both poems use different structural devices to convey their themes. "The Waste Land" is divided into distinct sections, each with its own image and tone, while "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" is structured as a series of fragmented thoughts. In "The Waste Land," Eliot's use of multiple voices and textual references creates a sense of fragmentation and disconnection, highlighting the way in which modern society has lost touch with its past. In contrast, "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" uses repetition and fragmentation to create a sense of isolation and frustration, highlighting the individual's struggle to find meaning and purpose in the modern world.

In conclusion, while both "The Waste Land" and "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" explore the theme of disillusionment and fragmentation, they do so through different poetic devices. Eliot's vivid and complex imagery in "The Waste Land" creates a bleak and desolate landscape, while the more understated imagery in "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" creates a sense of introspection and uncertainty. Similarly, the structural devices used in each poem create different effects, with "The Waste Land" highlighting the disconnection and fragmentation of modern society and "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock" highlighting the individual struggle to find meaning and purpose.

On the other hand, in "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock," there is a more subdued and introspective use of imagery. For example, in the lines "When the evening is spread out against the sky / Like a patient etherized upon a table," Eliot uses the metaphor of anesthesia to express Prufrock's sense of paralysis and detachment from the world around him. This image suggests the idea that the world has lost its vibrancy and become flat and lifeless.

Both poems also employ water imagery to convey their themes. In "The Waste Land," water is often associated with death and decay. For example, in the section "Death by Water," Eliot writes: "A current under sea / Picked his bones in whispers. / As he rose and fell / He passed the stages of his age and youth / Entering the whirlpool." The image of water as a form of death and decay is extended throughout the poem to convey the fragmentation and spiritual emptiness of modernity.

In contrast, in "The Love Song of J. Alfred Prufrock," water is used to create a sense of stagnation and isolation. For example, in the lines "In the room the women come and go / Talking of Michelangelo. / The yellow fog that rubs its back upon the window-panes, / The yellow smoke that rubs its muzzle on the window-panes, / Licked its tongue into the corners of the evening," Eliot creates a sense of dreariness and isolation by describing the city as being enveloped in a yellow fog that obscures the view of the outside world.

Overall, these examples of imagery show how both poems use distinct images to create different moods and convey their respective themes of disillusionment and fragmentation.

instruction: Provide a step-by-step guide for creating a savory vegetarian quiche that features a variety of cheeses and seasonal vegetables as the main ingredients. Be sure to include instructions for crafting the perfect buttery crust and preparing the filling, as well as any suggested optional additions or modifications to tailor the recipe to individual dietary preferences.
output:
Ingredients:
- For the crust:
   * 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour
   * 1/2 teaspoon salt
   * 1/2 cup unsalted butter, chilled and cubed
   * 3-4 tablespoons ice water
- For the filling:
   * 1 tablespoon olive oil
   * 1/2 cup diced onion
   * 2 garlic cloves, minced
   * 2 cups mixed vegetables (spinach, broccoli, zucchini, bell peppers), chopped
   * 4 large eggs
   * 1 cup milk or non-dairy milk (almond or soy milk)
   * 1/2 cup grated cheddar cheese
   * 1/2 cup grated Parmesan cheese
   * Salt and pepper to taste

Instructions:

1. Prepare the crust by combining flour and salt in a large bowl. Add chilled butter and use a pastry cutter or your fingers to mix until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. Gradually add ice water, one tablespoon at a time, until the dough comes together in a ball.
2. Flatten the dough into a disk and wrap in plastic wrap. Chill it in the fridge for 30 minutes while you prepare the filling.
3. Preheat the oven to 375°F.
4. In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté onions and garlic for 2-3 minutes until soft. Add the chopped vegetables and cook for 5-7 minutes until they are tender. Set aside.
5. In a mixing bowl, whisk eggs and milk together. Add in cheddar and Parmesan cheese and season with salt and pepper.
6. Roll out the chilled dough on a floured surface and fit it into a 9-inch pie dish. Trim the edges and prick the bottom with a fork.
7. Layer the cooked vegetables on top of the crust. Pour the egg mixture on top of the vegetables.
8. Bake for 35-45 minutes or until the filling is set and the crust is golden brown. Allow to cool for 5-10 minutes.
9. Slice and serve hot, garnished with additional grated cheese and/or fresh herbs.

Optional additions or modifications:
- Add sliced mushrooms, asparagus, or cherry tomatoes to the filling.
- Substitute dairy cheese with vegan cheese or omit it altogether for a vegan version.
- Add herbs like basil, parsley, or thyme to the filling for added flavor.

You may need to adjust the amount of liquid slightly if you use a different type of flour.

instruction: Can you explain the difference between white, brown, and wild rice, and how are they processed?
output:
White rice is the most common and very popular in many parts of the world. It is milled and polished to remove the bran and germ, which results in the loss of nutrients, fiber, and taste. This makes white rice easier to store, cook, and digest. White rice is usually more affordable and cooks faster than other types of rice.

Brown rice is considered to be a healthier option than white rice. Unlike white rice, it is not processed as much and retains the bran and germ, which contains fiber, vitamins, and minerals. Brown rice has a nutty flavor and chewy texture. Because of the bran, it takes longer to cook than white rice but provides more nutritional value.

Wild rice isn't technically rice but is actually a type of grass seed. It's a gluten-free grain that is high in fiber and minerals. It has a nutty flavor and chewy texture, much like brown rice. Wild rice is harder to find and more expensive than other types of rice. It takes longer to cook than white or brown rice due to its hard outer shell and can sometimes require soaking before cooking.

In summary, white rice is the most common and processed to remove the bran and germ to make it easier to store and cook. Brown rice retains the bran and germ, providing more nutritional value but takes longer to cook. Wild rice is a type of grass seed that is gluten-free and high in fiber and minerals, but it takes the longest to cook.

instruction: I normally eat white rice, but after hearing about the nutritional benefits of brown rice, I might switch. Is it difficult to cook?

Cooking brown rice is not difficult, but it takes a longer time to cook than white rice. Brown rice has a chewy texture, and its flavor is nutty.

To cook brown rice, simply rinse it using a fine-mesh sieve and drain the water. In a medium pot, add the washed brown rice and 2 cups of water (or broth). Bring the pot to boil, then reduce the heat to low and cover the pot with a tight-fitting lid. Simmer the rice for 40-50 minutes without uncovering the lid. After that, take the pot from the heat and let it sit for another 5-10 minutes. Then, fluff the rice with a fork.

Note that the cooking time may vary depending on the brand and type of brown rice. Also, you can add salt or any other herbs and spices to your preference while cooking the rice.

instruction: Design and implement a recommendation engine using machine learning algorithms that is able to suggest products to users based on their browsing and purchase history, as well as their demographics and interests. The recommendation engine should be integrated seamlessly into the e-commerce website and provide users with personalized product suggestions that increase engagement and conversions. The engine should also be scalable and adaptable, able to learn and improve over time as new user data is collected. Finally, the recommendation engine should be designed with the end user in mind, providing intuitive and user-friendly recommendations that are both accurate and helpful.
output:
To begin building a recommendation engine, here are the key steps:

1. Data Collection: Collect and maintain user data that includes browsing history, purchase history, demographic information, and interests.

2. Data Preprocessing: Preprocess the data by cleaning and transforming it to be used by machine learning algorithms.

3. Feature Extraction: Extract features from the user data such as clickstream data, search queries, and purchase history.

4. Recommendation Algorithms: Use machine learning algorithms such as collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, and hybrid filtering to build a recommendation engine that suggests products to users.

5. Evaluation Metrics: Use evaluation metrics such as accuracy, precision, and recall to evaluate the performance of the recommendation engine.

6. Integration: Integrate the recommendation engine into the e-commerce website so that it provides personalized product suggestions to users.

7. Testing and Improvement: Continuously test and improve the recommendation engine by collecting user feedback and updating the algorithms with new data. 

Overall, the recommendation engine should be designed to constantly learn and adapt to user behavior through data collection and analysis, providing an optimal user experience that promotes engagement and conversions.

instruction: Thank you for the detailed steps on building a recommendation engine. Can you please provide more information on the types of machine learning algorithms that are commonly used for recommendation engines? Also, how can I ensure that the recommendations provided by the engine are intuitive and user-friendly?
output:
Sure, here are some common machine learning algorithms used for recommendation engines:

1. Collaborative Filtering: This algorithm analyzes a user's interactions with similar users, looking for patterns in their behavior or item preferences. Then it recommends products based on what similar users have purchased in the past.

2. Content-Based Filtering: This algorithm recommends products primarily based on the user's historical interactions with the content. It analyses the items a user has already shown an interest in, and then recommends other items with similar attributes.

3. Hybrid Filtering: This algorithm combines both collaborative and content-based filtering to provide more accurate recommendations. 

To ensure that the recommendations provided by the engine are intuitive and user-friendly, here are a few tips to follow:

1. Choose an algorithm that is interpretable so that you can explain how the recommendation is being made.

2. Display the recommendations in a user-friendly format that is easy to understand and act upon.

3. Provide additional context to the user about why a particular product is being recommended, such as highlighting key features or reviews.

4. Allow the user to personalize their experience by providing options to adjust their preferences, select or filter recommendations, and provide feedback on recommendations. 

By following these tips, you can make sure that the recommendations provided by your engine are not only accurate but also user-friendly and helpful.

instruction: What are some proven strategies one can use to overcome procrastination and get things done in a timely manner?
output:
Some proven strategies to overcome procrastination are:

1. Set specific goals and deadlines: Assign a specific target or deadline to yourself, that will help to prioritize the task and plan accordingly.

2. Break tasks into smaller parts: Break down the task you're working on into smaller and manageable parts, so it doesn't seem 'too big' and you can approach it more confidently.

3. Use a timer: Set a timer for a determined period of time, helping you to stay focused on the task at hand and avoid distractions.

4. Eliminate distractions: Identify the factors that tend to distract you and remove those things to stay focused on the task.

5. Work in intervals: Work in intervals of 25-30 minutes and take a 5-minute break after each interval.

6. Reward yourself: Allocate an incentive for completing specific tasks.

7. Find an accountability partner: Partner up with someone who can keep a check on your progress and make sure you're on track.

8. Use visualization techniques: Visualize the successful completion of the task to stay motivated.

9. Get started: Sometimes getting started is the hardest part, so the best thing is just to start, even if you don't feel like it.

instruction: I always seem to get distracted by social media and end up procrastinating. Do you have any specific tips for overcoming this type of distraction?

3. Keep your phone on silent: Mute notifications on your phone so you're not distracted by them while working.

4. Remove social media apps: Remove social media apps from your phone or move them to a separate folder to reduce their visibility.

5. Take social media breaks: Schedule breaks to use social media between work sessions.

6. Use accountability tools: Use an accountability tool or app that tracks your time spent on social media.

7. Find a social media-free workspace: Choose a workspace free from distractions, with no social media access.

8. Focus on the task at hand: Stay focused on your work and remind yourself of your goals and priorities.

Remember, eliminating distractions requires discipline and self-control, so start with making small adjustments to your habits and gradually build up.

instruction: It's quite informative. I was wondering if you could add more information about the impact of public transportation on the environment and how it affects personal health. Specifically, I'm curious about how choosing public transportation over private vehicles can reduce greenhouse gas emissions and contribute to a cleaner environment. Can you provide more details on this topic?
output:
Certainly! One of the most significant benefits of using public transportation for personal health is its environmental impact. Public transportation usage can decrease greenhouse gas emissions and contribute to a cleaner environment, which, in turn, can positively impact personal health. Here are a few key points to consider:

Public Transportation's Role in Reducing Greenhouse Gas Emissions

- Greenhouse gas emissions, mainly carbon dioxide (CO2), are a significant contributor to climate change. The transportation sector is responsible for a significant portion of these emissions. - Personal vehicles are a significant source of transportation-related greenhouse gas emissions. According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), transportation accounted for 29% of greenhouse gas emissions in the United States in 2019, with cars and light trucks accounting for 58% of those emissions. - Public transportation, on the other hand, produces fewer emissions per passenger-mile than personal vehicles. According to the American Public Transportation Association, a person commuting by public transit can reduce his or her carbon footprint by 4,800 pounds of CO2 per year when switching from personal vehicles to public transportation. - Public transportation can also reduce congestion on roads, which can reduce emissions. Congestion creates more greenhouse gas emissions because cars and trucks sit in traffic and consume more fuel. - Electric public transit vehicles further contribute to lowering greenhouse gas emissions because they do not produce any emissions directly. Even in areas with higher carbon intensity from electricity production, electric vehicles are more efficient than internal combustion engine vehicles, and the emissions are still lower. Environmental Impact on Personal Health

- Air pollution, mainly from vehicles, is a significant cause of respiratory problems, such as asthma and lung cancer. Air pollution can also worsen existing health conditions, such as heart disease and COPD. - Diesel engines, found in some public transit systems such as buses, emit particulate matter, which can lead to respiratory and heart diseases. However, advancements in diesel engine technology have reduced emissions by up to 90% over the past few decades. - Electric public transit vehicles, as mentioned above, produce no direct emissions and can help reduce air pollution in urban areas, where congestion and air pollution are prevalent. - Green spaces, such as parks and gardens, also contribute to cleaner air by reducing air pollution. Public transportation also provides access to these areas. - By choosing public transportation over personal vehicles, individuals can contribute to reducing air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions, leading to better environmental conditions and personal health outcomes. In conclusion, choosing public transportation over personal vehicles can positively impact the environment and personal health. Public transportation produces fewer emissions per passenger-mile, reducing greenhouse gas emissions, and resulting in cleaner air, which can positively impact respiratory and heart health. Furthermore, increased use of public transportation can contribute to reduced traffic congestion and improve access to green spaces, further contributing to a cleaner and healthier environment.

instruction: This report is quite informative. Thank you for including the environmental impact of public transportation on personal health. I am interested in learning more about the technological advancements made in electric public transit vehicles. Can you provide me with more information on this topic, including the potential benefits and drawbacks of using electric public transit vehicles?
output:
Certainly! Electric public transit vehicles are a promising and rapidly evolving technology that has the potential to revolutionize public transportation. Here are some details on electric public transit vehicles, including potential benefits and drawbacks:

Electric Public Transit Vehicles

- Electric public transit vehicles use electricity as their primary energy source, either from an internal battery or an overhead electric wire.
- The primary benefit of electric public transit vehicles is their environmental friendliness. Electric vehicles produce zero tailpipe emissions, which makes them an excellent option for reducing air pollution, noise pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions.
- Further, electric vehicles require less maintenance than traditional vehicles since they have fewer mechanical parts.
- Electric public transit vehicles can also save transit operators significant amounts of money on fuel costs over the vehicle's lifespan. Electric vehicles have much lower per mile fueling costs than gasoline or diesel-powered vehicles, leading to considerable cost savings.
- In addition, electric public transit vehicles are much quieter and smoother than traditional vehicles, leading to a more comfortable riding experience for passengers.

Potential Benefits of Using Electric Public Transit Vehicles

- Advanced electric vehicle technology enables public transit vehicles to operate with greater efficiency than traditional fossil fuel vehicles. This efficiency is due to the capability to reclaim energy when brakes are applied and store electrical power in the vehicle's battery.
- Greenhouse gas emissions associated with energy production are reduced when electricity comes from renewable resources. This also reduces greenhouse gas emissions from the electricity grid, which contributes significantly to climate change.
- Electric public transit vehicles can integrate with the energy management system which allows them to become a part of a Smart Grid. This advanced technology can help stabilize the grid by charging when electricity demand is low and selling electricity back to the grid when demand is high.
- The reduced emissions from electric public transit vehicles can also result in improved health outcomes for people using public transportation, particularly those with respiratory illnesses.

Potential Drawbacks of Using Electric Public Transit Vehicles

- Although the technology is improving, the initial cost of acquiring electric public transit vehicles is high, which can be a significant barrier to widespread adoption.
- Electric public transit vehicles also require a robust charging infrastructure to support the fleet. Installing charging stations and power infrastructure can also be costly.
- Additionally, electric public transit vehicles have range limitations and require a charging stop between routes. This can lead to longer travel times for certain routes or delays due to the need for recharging.
- Battery deterioration over time may also pose a problem for electric public transit vehicles. This means that the vehicles may not be able to travel as far as newer vehicles and could require battery replacements, which can be costly.

Conclusion

Electric public transit vehicles have significant potential as a means of providing cleaner, more efficient, and cost-effective public transportation. The benefits include reduced greenhouse gas emissions, lower fuel costs, and a more comfortable and quiet riding experience. However, the high initial cost, range limitations, and charging infrastructure requirements of electric public transit vehicles can also pose challenges. Overall, continued advancements in technology and infrastructure may help overcome these challenges, leading to expanded use of electric public transit vehicles in the future.

instruction: Can you suggest the most-visited historical monument in Rome, Italy and its significance to the local culture?
output: The most-visited historical monument in Rome, Italy is the Colosseum. The Colosseum is a symbol of the city of Rome and its history. It is an ancient amphitheatre built in AD 80-90 and is famous for its gladiatorial contests and public spectacles such as animal hunts, mock sea battles, and dramas. The Colosseum is a remarkable example of the advanced engineering skills of the ancient Romans and is considered one of the greatest feats of architecture and engineering of the ancient world. Today, the Colosseum is a major tourist attraction and an important cultural and historical landmark in Rome, attracting millions of visitors each year. The significance of the Colosseum to the local culture lies in its history and its depiction of ancient Roman society, art, and architecture. The Colosseum represents not only the grandeur and power of ancient Rome, but also the cruelty and barbarism of its entertainment industry.

instruction: That's really interesting, I had no idea about the history behind the Colosseum. Do people still use it for events today?
output: No, the Colosseum is not used for events today. It hasn't been used for gladiatorial contests or any other kind of public event since ancient times. In fact, due to its age and state of preservation, it is not safe to hold events in the Colosseum. However, the monument is still used for special occasions, such as lighting displays and concerts, but they are held outside the structure itself. The Colosseum is now mainly a museum and a popular tourist destination, where people from all over the world come to learn about ancient Roman history and architecture.

instruction: Could you elaborate on the impact of Greek and Roman influence on Turkish art and music?
output:
The Greek and Roman influence on Turkish art and music can be traced back to the ancient times when Turkey was known as Anatolia. The Hellenistic culture and Roman civilization left a significant mark on the art and music of Turkey.

In the field of art, the Greeks introduced the concept of realistic human forms, and their sculpture and pottery were highly influential on the Turkish art scene. The Roman Empire brought monumental architecture and engineering techniques that can be seen in Turkey's historical sites, such as the ruins of Ephesus and the Hagia Sophia.

In the realm of music, the ancient Greeks developed a style of music called the modal system, which acted as a foundation for Turkish music. The Greeks also introduced the lyre, a stringed instrument that was later adapted into the Turkish saz. The Romans brought the concept of amphitheaters, where music and performances were held, and this idea was later adapted into the Ottoman Empire's classical music system.

During the Ottoman Empire, which spanned from the 14th to the early 20th century, Turkish art and music evolved and flourished due to the influence of numerous civilizations, including the Greeks and Romans. Ottoman artwork and architecture often featured intricate designs and mosaics, which were also present in ancient Greek and Roman art.

In conclusion, the impact of Greek and Roman influence on Turkish art and music has been significant and profound. It helped shape Turkish culture and gave rise to unique art and music forms that are still enjoyed today.

instruction: That's really interesting! Are there any specific examples of Greek or Roman influence in modern Turkish art or music?
output:
Yes, there are specific examples of Greek and Roman influence in modern Turkish art and music. One such example is the traditional Turkish folk music, which has its roots in both the Byzantine Empire and ancient Greece. The musical forms such as Gazel, Semai, and Taksim which were in use in court music during the Ottoman Empire, were influenced by the music of Ancient Greece.

Additionally, the concept of realism and the use of human figures in art can be seen in the works of modern Turkish artists. For instance, Turkish artist Bedri Rahmi Eyüboğlu was known for his use of vivid colors in his paintings, and his work often featured human forms, which can be traced back to the influence of Ancient Greek art.

Another example is the ancient Roman aqueducts that were built in Turkey, which served as a source of inspiration for Turkish artist Mehmet Aksoy when he created his sculpture called "The Monument of Humanity." The sculpture features a series of human faces and figures, which are carved into a large stone structure and resemble the arches of an aqueduct.

In modern Turkish architecture, the influence of ancient Greek and Roman architecture can also be seen. The use of columns, pediments, and dome structures was heavily influenced by the ancient Greeks and Romans, and these elements can be seen in modern Turkish buildings such as the Grand Bazaar and the Hagia Sophia.

Overall, the Greek and Roman influence on Turkish art and music is still present today, and it continues to shape Turkey's rich cultural heritage.

instruction:
With Captain Marvel and DC’s Shazam! hitting cinemas so close together many people have become aware that the two characters are in some way linked. Indeed, the fact that Shazam once went by the name Captain Marvel is no longer a secret held by the most ardent of comic book readers. However, just in case you aren’t familiar with the whole story, it does take place over the course of decades, here’s a handy guide to the history of the Captain Marvel name.
Interestingly, the name Captain Marvel predates both Marvel and DC in their current guises. Created by C. C. Beck and Bill Parker for Fawcett Comics in 1939, when Marvel was still Timely Comics and DC was a few years away from the merger of National Allied Publications and Detective Comics Inc., the character proved to be a big hit throughout the ‘Golden Age’ of comics in the 1940s and ’50s.
As the character gained popularity, however, the similarities between Fawcett’s much-admired hero and DC’s Superman became difficult to ignore. At this time DC was taking an aggressive stance on copyright infringement and forced Fawcett to cease publication in 1953. Despite the demise of Fawcett, it was another 19 years before DC would acquire the rights to the character during which time Marvel Comics had produced their own Captain Marvel title. When DC moved to return its version of the character to publication they were faced with a trademarking issue concerning the hero that Marvel Comics had been featuring for the previous five years.
Not to be deterred, DC re-published their hero under the title Shazam! in 1972, drawing inspiration from the character’s transformative cry from his Fawcett days. You’d expect this to bring an end to the already complicated story, but you’d be wrong. During the character’s Fawcett run in the ’40s and ’50s an entire family of ‘Marvel’ characters were created and later acquired by DC. So, even though DC can’t use the name Captain Marvel to refer to the original hero, they do have the characters Mary Marvel and Captain Marvel Jr. On their books. It makes for an interesting situation given that the publisher continues to use these characters ensuring that Shazam! can never be distanced from his original moniker. With the launch of the New 52! comic series in 2011, however, the publisher officially began to call the character Shazam but comics fans aren’t going to let a little thing like that get in the way of a good debate.
Things don’t get much clearer over at Marvel Comics either, with the Captain Marvel name causing all sorts of continuity issues there as well. When the company created its version in 1967 as the Kree spy Mar’Vell, the character retained a number of the characteristics of the Fawcett original. However, Marvel’s Mar’Vell didn’t really take off with fans in its early years but by 1977 had gathered a sufficient following to warrant the launch of a spin-off series helmed by the female hero Ms. Marvel. That character had appeared in alongside Captain Marvel intermittently since 1978. Captain Marvel and Ms. Marvel would continue to coexist until well into the twenty-first century before Carol Danvers (Ms. Marvel) took on the Captain Marvel title following the death of Mar’Vell in 2012. As readers will no doubt be aware, for the 2019 Captain Marvel movie Mar’Vell was reimagined as a female Kree scientist, with Carol Danvers becoming the first person to use the Captain Marvel moniker.
And there you have it. Shazam is Captain Marvel but can’t be called Captain Marvel for legal reasons, and Mar’Vell in many ways shares the same origin as Shazam! but can use the Captain Marvel name. Only, he died in 2012 and the name passed on to Carol Danvers, who was Ms. Marvel but is now Captain Marvel. Then somewhere between the comic pages and the MCU Mar’Vell became female and not-Captain Marvel and Carol Danvers became Captain Marvel but was never Ms. Marvel. Simple really.
Who is your favourite Captain Marvel? Let us know!
What legal issues did DC face when trying to publish their version of Captain Marvel and how did they overcome it?
output: DC faced a trademarking issue when they tried to republish their version of Captain Marvel, as Marvel Comics had already been featuring a character with that name for the previous five years. DC then chose to publish their hero under the title Shazam! in 1972, drawing inspiration from the character’s transformative cry from his Fawcett days. They were also able to keep the characters Mary Marvel and Captain Marvel Jr., who were part of the original Fawcett family of ‘Marvel’ characters that DC had acquired.

instruction: Can you tell me more about the history of the captain marvel name and how it has caused continuity issues in the marvel comics universe?
output:
Sure! The history of the Captain Marvel name is quite complicated. The character, created by C.C. Beck and Bill Parker for Fawcett Comics in 1939, was initially called Captain Marvel and proved to be a big hit throughout the ‘Golden Age’ of comics in the 1940s and ’50s. However, DC Comics took an aggressive stance on copyright infringement and forced Fawcett to cease publication in 1953 due to similarities between Captain Marvel and DC's Superman. 

Fast forward to 1967, Marvel Comics introduced their own version of Captain Marvel, who was a Kree spy named Mar-Vell. Marvel’s Mar-Vell retained many of the characteristics of the Fawcett original, but didn't really take off with fans in its early years. By 1977, a female hero named Ms. Marvel appeared in the Marvel comics universe, and eventually, she took on the Captain Marvel mantle following the death of Mar’Vell in 2012. 

Meanwhile, DC Comics reacquired the rights to the original Captain Marvel character in 1972 but was forced to publish under the title "Shazam!" due to a trademarking issue. While DC couldn’t use the name Captain Marvel to refer to the original hero, they still owned the characters Mary Marvel and Captain Marvel Jr., who were part of the original Fawcett family of ‘Marvel’ characters. 

All of this means that the Captain Marvel name has caused continuity issues in both the DC Comics and Marvel Comics universes. Even with the launch of DC Comics' New 52! comic series in 2011, which officially began to call their hero by the name Shazam, comics fans still debate the issue. Similarly, Marvel Comics has had to navigate the legacy of the Captain Marvel name, with Carol Danvers (Ms. Marvel) eventually becoming the new Captain Marvel. 

Overall, the history of the Captain Marvel name is complicated, and it has led to some interesting developments in the comics world.

instruction: What are some of the sociocultural factors that may contribute to farmers' reluctance to embrace new technologies, and how can they be addressed?
output:
1. Educational Factors: Farmers who lack formal education or have minimal exposure to technology may have difficulty adopting new technologies. They may not see the value or understand how it can increase production. Encouraging education and training programs can benefit farmers to learn about new technologies and apply them to their operations.

2. Traditional Farming Practices: Many farmers have a long-standing tradition of agriculture passed from generation to generation. They may be reluctant to change the way of doing things that has worked for them. Providing support in the form of exposure visits to progressive farmers, trial plots, and training can help farmers learn about new technologies.

3. Cost: Cost can be a hindrance to the adoption of new technologies. Many farmers may not be able to afford the high cost of new technology. Government programs, subsidies, and grants can support farmers' initial investments in technology.

4. Perception & Attitude: Farmers may have a negative perception of the technology, distrust towards the product or its maker. Educating farmers on the benefits and risks of technology and confidence-building measures to address inherent issues can help to change the farmers' perception towards technology.

5. Social Networks: Farmers depend on social networks for advice and support. Peer-to-peer influence can be a powerful motivator or a hindrance to technology adoption. Therefore, encouraging farmers to experiment with new technologies in a limited space or incentive schemes to create a positive word of mouth can be helpful.

6. Access to Information: Access to information is vital in technology adoption. Availability of information through a mobile app or a helpline service can help farmers to stay updated and get their queries addressed in real-time.

Providing a combination of incentives, educational programs, communication, and access to information can help farmers to embrace new technologies.

instruction: Do you think there are any cultural factors that contribute to farmers' reluctance to adopt new technologies?
output: Yes, there are cultural factors that contribute to farmers' reluctance to adopt new technologies. Culturally ingrained beliefs and practices associated with agriculture can lead to resistance towards change. For instance, certain cultures may view technology as a disruption of nature's balance, so farmers may be hesitant to use them. Additionally, farmers may prioritize the preservation of tradition over innovation, leading to resistance towards adopting new technologies. Cultural factors can be addressed by engaging with communities and understanding their concerns and beliefs. Innovators can work with community leaders to find inclusive and culturally sensitive ways to introduce new technologies that enhance, rather than disrupt, traditional agricultural practices.

instruction: Write a mystery short story about a missing person case in which the victim disappeared without a trace, and the only clues left behind are cryptic messages and ominous symbols. Use a third-person limited point of view to build suspense and increase the emotional impact of the story, and consider employing red herrings and plot twists to keep the reader guessing until the very end. Additionally, explore the psychological implications of disappearance and investigate the motives and possible suspects through the eyes of the protagonist, a detective or an investigative journalist driven by their thirst for truth and justice.
output:
Detective Mark was assigned to a new case that would challenge his investigative skills. A young woman named Emily was missing, and there were no signs of a struggle or any indication of where she could have gone. The only clues left behind were ominous symbols and cryptic messages that led to dead-end after another.

With no leads, Mark found himself visiting the last known person to have seen Emily alive, her boyfriend, Joe. Joe was visibly shaken and claimed to have no idea about her whereabouts. They were planning a surprise birthday party for Emily, and he had no reason to believe she would just disappear.

However, while interviewing Joe, Mark noticed odd behavior from one of his roommates, Steve. When questioned about the situation, Steve was quick to deflect and became quite defensive. Mark made a mental note to keep a closer eye on him.

The investigation continued, and every lead seemed to circle back to the same cryptic symbols and ominous messages left behind. Digging deeper, Mark discovered that Emily had been dabbling in alternative religions, including witchcraft and sorcery, which initially provided a plausible explanation for the symbols.

But as time went on and more research was done, the symbols began to take on a new, sinister meaning. They were connected to a cult-like organization that specialized in kidnapping and human trafficking. Could Emily have gotten involved with this group? Could she have become another victim?

The investigation took a dark turn as Mark tried to track down anyone involved with the organization, but they were shrouded in secrecy. One night, Mark received a call from Joe, the last person to see Emily alive. Joe had received a cryptic message that seemed to come from Emily, leading them to an abandoned warehouse on the outskirts of town.

Mark arrived on the scene quickly, armed and ready for whatever lay ahead. As he entered the warehouse, he heard a eerie sound in the distance, drawing him deeper into the darkness. Suddenly, Mark was surrounded by the cult members, and he realized too late that the message was a trap. He had been lured into a trap to rescue Emily, only to find himself at the mercy of the very people he was investigating.

Mark narrowly escaped, but Emily was gone, and the only thing left behind was a cryptic symbol on the wall. With no more leads and no hope of finding Emily, Mark realized he had let his personal mission for truth and justice cloud his judgment.

The case was officially filed as unsolved, and Mark walked away, haunted by the mysteries that surround the disappearance of Emily. He never forgot her, and every time he saw a cryptic symbol or ominous message, he thought of the young woman who disappeared without a trace, and the strange and mysterious cult who were behind it all.

instruction: The story you've generated is quite intriguing, but I feel like there could be more information about the cult and their motives. Can you provide more details about them and how they operate?
output:
Certainly, let me expand on that aspect of the story:

Mark discovered that the cult was based on a twisted ideology that believed in the superiority of the chosen few and that the rest of humanity was expendable. They believed that they were doing the world a service by capturing young, bright, and beautiful individuals and offering them as human sacrifices to their so-called divine ruler.

Their recruitment and initiation process was subtle and often involved grooming and brainwashing techniques that slowly eroded the will of their victims. After years of conducting kidnappings, they had mastered the art of hiding their presence and leaving little to no evidence of their activities.

Their operations were controlled from a remote location, with hierarchies responsible for different tasks. This made it challenging to track down and halt their activities as authorities put immense effort into infiltrating the organization or tracing any possible leads.

It was a frustrating reality for Mark and his team, but they remained steadfast in their pursuit, hoping to save other potential victims from the clutches of this organization.

instruction:
Given the text: In 2008 Paula Apsell phoned Powderhouse Productions, a Boston-area production company, and uttered a sentence that most likely had never been spoken before (or since) by any executive producer in the history of television: “We want to make four hours about Materials Science”. For those unfamiliar with the term, Materials Science is exactly what it sounds like — the study of basic materials. Universities with Materials Science departments offer classes with titles like “Reinforced Concrete” & “Microstructural Dynamics.” The challenge of turning this topic into an entertaining TV series probably ranks as just slightly easier than attempting to make a feature doc about the color beige. But nevertheless, it is science and so by definition, as far as Paula was concerned, there ought to be a story embedded somewhere in the topic. What resulted was the successful and popular mini-series called Making Stuff.
Today, the toughest challenges we face at NOVA aren’t always topic driven. And for that reason, this award could not come at a better time. As Paula often repeats: science and science journalism are under siege as never before. At NOVA we all feel it acutely. That’s partly why it’s so important to recognize Paula’s willingness to tackle tough topics and tell stories aimed at general audiences in an effort to raise science literacy and promote critical thinking among the millions of viewers who tune in or stream the programs made by NOVA’s indefatigable filmmakers.
Not many broadcasters would have the temerity to tackle string theory in “The Elegant Universe” or the theory of General Relativity in a film like “Inside Einstein’s Mind,” which premiered on the 100th anniversary of the publication of that world-altering theory. Likewise, there aren’t many who would commission a two-hour film about the least visible objects in the universe — black holes — finding a way to make them visible by hitching a ride on the imaginations and passions of the physicists and astronomers who study them. Not to mention, simultaneously showcasing the outsized contributions of women scientists working in the field. And in recent years, Paula has found purpose in probing the intersection of science and social justice — commissioning films like “Poisoned Water” about the Flint water crisis, a film honored this year with an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Science and Technology Documentary.
Over her long career Paula has provided a platform for great science communicators, whether as protagonists in quests to solve mysteries, or as hosts like Neil DeGrasse Tyson, David Pogue, Kirk Johnson, Janna Levin or Brian Greene. It’s editorial choices like these that challenge public perceptions of science as remote or inaccessible, and reveal instead the inherent drama and beauty of the human struggle to understand the natural world.
This ever-evolving, eclectic mix of stories across all facets of science, engineering, history and the natural world are what NOVA is known for and is responsible for keeping NOVA at the forefront of science journalism for 45 years — fully 2/3rds of that history, we note, with Paula’s hand firmly on the tiller. NOVA began in 1974 as an experiment inspired by the British science series Horizon. But under Paula’s leadership it has reached an ever-wider national and international audience to become the American icon that it is today. Over her long tenure, Paula has demonstrated a dedication to NOVA’s viewers that is unsurpassed among us. She tries to see the entirety of the world and current affairs of the day through the filter of science journalism; always on the lookout for the stories that will entertain and nourish our audience.
As Paula so often reminds us — science is not a thing. It is a story. It is an endeavor that has its roots in our fundamental humanity and in the curiosity we can trace to our primate ancestors. And each week NOVA proudly sets out to tell those stories.
We are so fortunate to have joined Paula Apsell in the eminently worthwhile work that NOVA has been doing for more than 40 years and we are looking forward to the decades to come.
Julia Cort is Deputy Executive Producer of NOVA.
Chris Schmidt is Senior Producer of NOVA.
Could you provide more details about the NOVA mini-series called "Making Stuff" and how it tackled the topic of Materials Science in an entertaining way?
output: The NOVA mini-series called "Making Stuff" was a four-hour program that tackled the topic of Materials Science in an entertaining way. The challenge was to make the complex topic of basic materials interesting to a general audience. The series explored the science and engineering behind everyday materials like metal, paper, and plastics, and how they are used in innovative ways. The program featured segments on a variety of topics, including bulletproof vests, lightweight metals used in aircraft, and smart materials that change properties based on external stimuli. The series was hosted by materials science expert and frequent NOVA contributor David Pogue, and included interviews with leading scientists and engineers in the field. Through engaging visuals and clear explanations, "Making Stuff" brought the world of materials science to life for a wide audience.

instruction: Can you provide examples of other tough topics tackled by NOVA under Paula Apsell's leadership?
output:
Under Paula Apsell's leadership, NOVA has tackled an array of tough topics. Some notable examples include:

1. String theory in "The Elegant Universe"
2. The theory of general relativity in "Inside Einstein's Mind"
3. The least visible objects in the universe - black holes - in a two-hour program
4. The intersection of science and social justice in "Poisoned Water" about the Flint water crisis
5. The science of climate change in "Decoding the Weather Machine"
6. The science behind addiction in "Addiction"
7. The science of human evolution in "Becoming Human"
8. The science of the human brain in "What Makes Us Human?" 
9. The science of genetics in "Cracking the Code of Life"

This demonstrates NOVA's commitment to producing high-quality science journalism that is accessible to a wide audience.

INT. PRISON YARD - DAY

Jack is approached by a burly inmate, SAM, who sizes him up and tries to start a fight.

What do you want, Sam?

JACK 
(surprised)

I am glad to report that we have completed the initial phases of the project, which included gathering requirements from different departments, identifying the potential vendors, and evaluating the different CRMs available in the market.

instruction: Develop and execute a comprehensive market research project to analyze the feasibility and effectiveness of introducing renewable energy products in the luxury hospitality segment. The study should include an assessment of market demand, competitive landscape, cost-benefit analysis, potential return on investment, and consumer behavior analysis. The final report should include clear recommendations for the development, positioning, and marketing of renewable energy products that meet the identified needs of luxury hospitality businesses. Use a mix of qualitative and quantitative research methods, including surveys, focus groups, interviews, and secondary research sources to gather and analyze data.
output:
Introduction

The hospitality industry is increasingly focused on incorporating sustainable practices into their businesses, one of which is the adoption of renewable energy sources. This research project aims to assess the feasibility and effectiveness of introducing renewable energy products in the luxury hospitality segment. The study is expected to provide a comprehensive analysis of the market demand, competitive landscape, cost-benefit analysis, potential return on investment, and consumer behavior analysis.

Research Methodology

The research will adopt both qualitative and quantitative research methods. Primary data will be collected through surveys, focus groups, and interviews with key stakeholders in the luxury hospitality industry. Secondary data will be collected through literature reviews, industry reports, and databases.

Sample Selection

The study will target luxury hotels and resorts in the United States, with a concentration on the East and West Coasts. The sample will comprise hotel managers, sustainability managers, and guests in the luxury hospitality segment.

Data Collection Methods

Surveys will be designed to collect data on market demand, consumer behavior, and customer preferences for renewable energy products. The surveys will be distributed through email and online platforms. Focus groups and interviews will be conducted with hotel and sustainability managers to gain insights on the competitive landscape, cost-benefit analysis, and potential return on investment.

Data Analysis

The data collected will be analyzed through descriptive analysis, correlation analysis, and regression analysis. Descriptive analysis will be used to analyze data on market demand, consumer behavior, and customer preferences. Correlation analysis will be used to measure the relationship between variables, such as customer satisfaction and the adoption of renewable energy products. Regression analysis will be used to identify significant predictors for the adoption of renewable energy products.

Expected Outcomes

The analysis of the data collected will provide insights into the feasibility and effectiveness of introducing renewable energy products in the luxury hospitality segment. The study is expected to identify the market demand for renewable energy products, competitive landscape, cost-benefit analysis, potential return on investment, and consumer behavior analysis.

Recommendations

Based on the results of the study, clear recommendations will be made for the development, positioning, and marketing of renewable energy products that meet the identified needs of luxury hospitality businesses. The recommendations will be tailored to the specific requirements and preferences of luxury hotels and resorts in the United States.

instruction: Please create a comprehensive guide consisting of detailed steps on how to build a professional website using either WordPress or any other CMS. The guide should include detailed instructions regarding the process of selecting a layout, theme, and relevant plugins, as well as incorporating customized content, images, videos, and multimedia items. Additionally, the guide should provide guidance regarding the creation of a navigation system, optimizing site speed and performance, and incorporating that site's SEO.
output:
Building a professional website can seem intimidating at first, but with the help of a content management system (CMS) such as WordPress, it's actually relatively straightforward. In this guide, we'll walk you through step-by-step on how to build a professional website using WordPress or another CMS.

Step 1: Choose a Domain and Hosting

The first step in building a website is to choose a domain and hosting provider. Your domain is your website's address, while hosting is where your website will be stored on the internet. When considering your domain and hosting options, make sure to choose a reliable provider with good uptime and customer support.

Step 2: Install WordPress or Another CMS

Once you have your domain and hosting set up, it's time to install WordPress or another CMS. Most hosting providers make it easy to install WordPress with just a few clicks. Follow the instructions provided by your hosting provider to install WordPress.

Step 3: Choose a Theme

The next step is to choose a theme for your website. A theme is like a template that determines the look and feel of your website. There are thousands of WordPress themes available, both free and paid. Choose a theme that aligns with your website's goals and brand identity.

Step 4: Install Relevant Plugins

Plugins are like apps for your WordPress website. They can help you add features such as social sharing buttons, contact forms, and more. Take a look at the plugins available and install ones that will make your website more functional and user-friendly.

Step 5: Add Customized Content

Now that you have your website framework set up, it's time to add customized content. This includes writing copy that speaks to your audience, adding images and videos, and more. Create pages that outline your services or products, and make sure your website reflects your brand identity throughout.

Step 6: Create a Navigation System

Your website navigation system is the menu that visitors use to access various pages on your website. Create a navigation system that is easy to use and makes it simple for visitors to find what they're looking for on your website.

Step 7: Optimize Site Speed and Performance

Slow-loading websites can negatively impact user experience and SEO. To optimize your site speed and performance, make sure to compress images, minify code, and use caching tools. You can also use a content delivery network (CDN) to improve load times.

Step 8: Incorporate SEO

Search engine optimization (SEO) is the process of optimizing your website for search engine visibility. To incorporate SEO into your website, make sure to use relevant keywords throughout your content, create descriptive meta tags and titles, and add alt text to images.

Conclusion

Building a professional website doesn't have to be difficult. With the help of a content management system like WordPress and the eight steps outlined above, you can create a website that is functional, user-friendly, and reflective of your brand identity.

instruction: Can you provide more detailed information on how to optimize site speed and performance? How do I compress images and minify code? Also, what is a content delivery network and how can it help with load times?
output: Sure, I'd be happy to provide more information on optimizing site speed and performance. Compress Images: Large images can slow down the load time of your website. To compress images, you can use image compression tools such as TinyPNG or Squoosh. These tools compress the size of your images without affecting their quality. Minify Code: Minifying code means removing unnecessary spaces, comments, and other characters from your code to reduce its size. This can help speed up your website's load time. To minify code, you can use plugins such as WP Fastest Cache, Autoptimize, or W3 Total Cache. Use Caching Tools: A caching tool can help speed up your website by storing a version of your website in a user's browser so they don't have to reload it every time they visit. Some popular caching tools include WP Fastest Cache, W3 Total Cache, and WP Super Cache. Content Delivery Network (CDN): A CDN is a network of servers located around the world that store copies of your website. When a user requests your website, the server closest to them will provide them with a copy of your website, reducing load time. Some popular CDN providers include Cloudflare, Amazon CloudFront, and StackPath. I hope this additional information helps you optimize your website's performance!

instruction: Write a narrative essay detailing the experience of a professional athlete with ADHD from the moment they wake up until the end of their day, describing their daily routine, challenges, and strategies for managing their symptoms both on and off the field. Use descriptive language and provide specific examples to illustrate the athlete's experience. Consider discussing how their condition affects their performance and relationships with teammates, coaches, and family members.
output:
I wake up to the sound of my alarm blaring, signaling the beginning of another day filled with challenges that I need to overcome. I am a professional athlete, but I also have ADHD, which means that my days are anything but normal.

As I get out of bed, I stretch and try to clear my mind of any distractions that may hinder my focus. I know that I need to take my medication at the same time every day, so I immediately go to the bathroom to take my pills. I then head to the kitchen to make breakfast. I know that eating a healthy and balanced meal is essential for my body and brain to function efficiently throughout the day.

After my meal, I take a few minutes to review my schedule for the day. I need to be mindful of my activities, as they require a tremendous amount of focus and stamina. I grab my sports bag that I packed the night before and head out for practice.

As I get on the field, I try to block out any external distractions that may take away from my concentration. Before every practice or game, I need to take a few extra minutes to mentally prepare myself. This involves setting short-term goals for myself, focusing on positive self-talk, and practicing visualization techniques. I need to work extra hard to ensure that my mind stays sharp and focused.

During practice, I have to be extra vigilant about staying on task. It's easy for me to get sidetracked, but I remind myself of the importance of staying on target. If I get distracted, I may miss crucial instructions given by my coach or miss cues from my teammates that could impact our performance.

Off the field, I know that staying organized is key to managing my ADHD. I use a planner and to-do list to stay focused and to prioritize my tasks. If I have too much on my plate, I know that I need to ask for help. I rely on my support network of family, friends, and coaches to keep me on task throughout the day.

At night, I take time to unwind and relax. I know that getting enough rest is critical to repairing my body and to ensure that I am in top physical and mental shape. I try to establish a routine, so that my body knows when it's time to wind down.

Dealing with ADHD while being a professional athlete is not easy, but it's possible. I use my condition as a driving force to push me to be the best athlete I can be. I have learned to accept that it's okay to ask for help, and I am grateful for the support that I have around me. I have also come to understand that my unique perspective can add value to my team and their success. I am confident that with my daily routine, strategies, and support network, I can overcome any challenges that come my way.

instruction: Write a how-to guide on creating zero-waste gift wrap.
output:
Creating zero-waste gift wrap is not only eco-friendly, but it also adds a personal touch to your gift-giving. Here is a step-by-step guide on how to create your very own zero-waste gift wrap:

1. Choose Your Materials
The first step in creating zero-waste gift wrap is to choose the materials you will use. You can use any material that can be reused, recycled, or composted. A few examples include:
- Fabric scraps
- Old newspaper or magazine
- Reusable shopping bags
- Brown paper bags
- Scrapbook paper
- Old maps or sheet music
- Tissue paper

2. Wrap Your Gift
Once you have chosen your materials, wrap your gift as you normally would. You can either use the traditional wrapping technique or try furoshiki, a Japanese method of wrapping gifts in fabric.

3. Decorate Your Gift
This is where the fun begins! You can add a personal touch to your gift by decorating it however you like. Here are some ideas to get you started:
- Tie a ribbon or twine around the gift
- Use natural materials such as leaves or twigs to adorn the gift
- Draw or write a personal message on the gift using markers or paint
- Use stamps or stencils to create a design on the gift
- Attach a small gift tag made from recycled paper

4. Deliver Your Gift
Finally, deliver your zero-waste gift to the recipient. Let them know that the gift wrap is reusable or compostable and ask them to pass it on to someone else or dispose of it responsibly.

By following these simple steps, you can create a beautiful, eco-friendly gift wrap that will make your gift stand out and show the recipient that you care about the environment.

instruction: It looks great. Can you tell me more about the furoshiki wrapping technique? I've never heard of that before.
output:
Sure, I'd be happy to! Furoshiki is a traditional Japanese method of wrapping gifts in fabric. The fabric is folded and tied in various ways to create a beautiful and unique wrapping for the gift. Here's how you can use the furoshiki technique for zero-waste gift wrapping:

1. Choose Your Fabric
Choose a piece of fabric that is large enough to wrap your gift. You can use any type of fabric, but a lightweight and sturdy fabric like cotton works well. You can also choose a fabric with a fun pattern or design to add an extra touch of flair. 2. Place the Gift in the Center
Lay your fabric flat on a table or flat surface and place your gift in the center. If your gift is an odd shape, you may need to fold the fabric around it a bit to get the right fit. 3. Wrap the Fabric Around the Gift
Take the opposite corners of the fabric and bring them up and over the gift. Tie them together in a knot at the top, making sure to leave enough slack to create a handle. 4. Fold the Remaining Corners
Take the remaining corners of the fabric and fold them over the knot at the top. Tie them together in a knot, making sure to leave enough slack to create another handle. 5. Adjust the Wrapping
Finally, adjust the fabric around the gift until it looks neat and attractive. You can tuck in any extra fabric or fluff out the handles to create a nice, finished look. By using the furoshiki technique, you can create a stunning and reusable wrapping for your gifts that is both eco-friendly and memorable. Experiment with different fabrics and knots to find the perfect wrapping for your next gift-giving occasion.

instruction: Examine the integration of artificial intelligence in creating art pieces that respond to environmental data.
output:
The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in creating art pieces that respond to environmental data is a rapidly growing trend in the art world. With the help of AI and machine learning algorithms, artists are creating pieces that evolve and change in response to changes in the environment, such as temperature, air quality, and sound. These works of art not only reflect the state of the environment but also raise awareness about issues like climate change and pollution.

One example of this is the "Data Garden" exhibit in Philadelphia, where plants were connected to sensors that monitored the surrounding air quality, soil moisture, and light levels. The data collected from these sensors was then translated into a musical composition, which changed and evolved as the environmental conditions changed.

Another example of AI integrated artwork is the work of Italian artist, Fabio Giampietro, and his series of paintings titled "Planet Pulse." The paintings were created using both traditional painting techniques and AI algorithms that analyzed satellite images of the earth's surface. The resulting artwork depicts mesmerizing landscapes of abstracted earth images with vibrant, pulsating colors.

instruction: What are the cultural attractions located near the University of Edinburgh?

4. The Scottish National Gallery - an art museum comprising a vast collection of contemporary and classic art exhibits. 

5. The Scottish Storytelling Centre - an intimate venue where you can experience live storytelling, music, and spoken-word performances. 

6. The Palace of Holyroodhouse - a royal residence located next to Edinburgh's stunning Holyrood Abbey. You can gaze at the lavish interiors, the state apartments, and the royal collections. 

7. The Royal Mile - a historic street in Edinburgh that connects Edinburgh Castle and Palace of Holyroodhouse. It has different shops, restaurants, and monuments that depict Scotland's rich history and culture. 

8. The Surgeon's Hall Museum - a unique medical museum that displays old medical equipment, specimens, and works by legendary medical figures. 

9. The Scottish Parliament Building - An iconic building with a unique modern design, located on the lower slope of Edinburgh's Royal Mile. 

10. The Festival Theatre - A leading theater in Scotland, hosting a variety of productions throughout the year, from classic Shakespearean plays to modern comedies.

instruction: Write step-by-step instructions for how to make an Italian sub sandwich with salami, ham, provolone cheese, lettuce, tomato, onion, pepperoncini, and Italian dressing, using a baguette as the bread. Be sure to include specific measurements and placement of ingredients, as well as any additional tips or variations on the classic recipe.
output:
Ingredients: 
- 1 baguette (about 12 inches)
- 4-6 slices of salami
- 4-6 slices of ham
- 4-6 slices of provolone cheese
- 4-6 leaves of lettuce
- 1 medium tomato, sliced
- 1/4 medium onion, sliced
- 4-6 pepperoncini peppers
- 2-3 tablespoons Italian dressing

Instructions:

1. Preheat your oven to 375°F.

2. Cut the baguette in half and lay it open on a baking sheet or a piece of aluminum foil.

3. Layer the salami on one side of the baguette, followed by the ham and then the provolone cheese on top.

4. Place the baking sheet in the oven and bake for about 5-7 minutes, or until the cheese is melted.

5. While the sandwich is toasting, prepare the vegetables. Wash and dry the lettuce leaves and tomatoes, and slice the onion thinly.

6. Once the cheese is melted, take the sandwich out of the oven and place the lettuce leaves on the other side of the baguette, followed by the tomato slices, onion slices, and pepperoncini peppers.

7. Drizzle 2-3 tablespoons of Italian dressing over the sandwich.

8. Close the sandwich by pressing the top half of the baguette down onto the bottom half.

9. Slice the sandwich into desired serving sizes.

Tips and variations:

- If you prefer your bread more toasted, bake the baguette halves in the oven for a few minutes before adding the sandwich toppings.
- Substitute or add other deli meats such as turkey, roast beef or mortadella.
- For added flavor, spread a thin layer of mustard or mayo on the baguette halves before adding the meat and cheese.
- You can also add other vegetables such as roasted red peppers, sliced olives or artichoke hearts.
- You can vary the amount of dressing or add other condiments such as mayo, mustard, or hot sauce.

instruction: Could you add some suggestions for sides or chips to serve with the sandwich?

- Potato chips, either plain or flavored
- Garlic knots or breadsticks
- Pasta salad or potato salad
- Coleslaw
- Pickles or pickled vegetables
- Roasted vegetables such as zucchini, eggplant, or bell peppers
- Fruit salad or sliced fruit such as apples or grapes
- A side of tomato soup or minestrone soup
- A small green salad with Italian dressing

You can also consider serving the sandwich with a cold beverage such as iced tea, lemonade or a cold beer. Enjoy!

instruction:
Three researchers in NSW share how they are working to change lives by reducing tobacco use across the state.
Associate Professor Gillian Gould is working from the Hunter New England region to help Aboriginal people quit smoking.
Throughout her career, A/Professor Gould has collaborated with Aboriginal communities to understand the best way to give culturally-appropriate support.
“It's vital to be working with Aboriginal communities. If you’re working on new strategies to help Aboriginal people quit, you can't really do it any other way,” she says.
A/Professor Gould is currently finalising recruitment for a national trial of 'SISTAQUIT' (Supporting Indigenous Smokers to Assist Quitting), which is training health providers to have consultations with pregnant Aboriginal women.
“A lot of young women in Aboriginal communities are smoking and, if they get pregnant, they might be experiencing a lot of difficulties and have a lot to deal with,” she explains.
Another research project A/Professor Gould is involved in is helping pregnant women quit smoking who are going through drug and alcohol clinics.
Professor Christine Paul is passionate about working in tobacco research, due to the personal impact that smoking has on the lives of people across Australia.
“Knowing that a lot of the suffering is preventable, drives me to keep working in tobacco control,” says the Professor of School of Medicine and Public Health (Health Behaviour Sciences) at the University of Newcastle.
A key area of research is now on smoking cessation support for people who have been diagnosed with cancer.
“A lot of people aren’t aware that it’s not too late to quit, even when you have cancer,” Professor Paul explains.
“In fact, for many people, they will be able to tolerate their cancer treatment better if they quit, and they will increase their chances of surviving cancer if they quit."
A new study led by Dr Flora Tzelepis from the University of Newcastle is aiming to break down barriers experienced by people outside metropolitan areas wanting to quit.
“This study will increase our understanding of which smoking cessation strategies are most beneficial in helping smokers in regional and remote areas to quit smoking,” she explains.
Male smoking rates in outer regional and remote NSW are more than 10 per cent higher than those in metropolitan areas. For women, the difference is almost 2.5 per cent.
The study is assessing the impact of different approaches to quit support, including online video sessions (e.g. Via Skype, Face Time), telephone support calls and written materials.
Dr Tzelepis believes video support sessions could help overcome issues, such as the distance and cost required to attend cessation services in regional and remote NSW.
To date, the study has recruited more than 470 people to be involved, and follow-up surveys that are assessing smoking cessation have also commenced.
People can still be involved in the trial – if you or someone you know lives in rural or regional NSW and would like to participate in this study, you can go to the study website, or contact Dr Tzelepis at Flora.Tzelepis@newcastle.edu.au or call (02) 4924 6275 to be involved.
The Cancer Institute NSW is proud to support researchers from across the state who are progressing how we help people quit smoking.
Learn more about how we’re working to reduce smoking rates across NSW.

output: Professor Christine Paul's research focus is on smoking cessation support for people who have been diagnosed with cancer.
